Resolved criterion records retain legacy URLs without pending-approval labels.

edits.old: Aveson challenges a universal causal inference from Heimbach. Absence of PM in nine negative TP-FNA cases does not establish safety. Soliman's occult-node recipients do not validate deliberate nodal expansion. One prospective pilot admitted regional lymphadenopathy in locally advanced hilar and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma; five of 18 reached transplantation and one had an isolated portacaval nodal recurrence at 12 months. Whether the nodes were proven malignant is not reported in the abstract, and it cannot validate a cleared-node stratum. The exact 3.0-cm boundary is a current policy boundary, not a biological discontinuity proven by these studies.

Whether the nodes were proven malignant is not reported in the abstract, and it cannot validate a cleared-node stratum.   "provenance": "Built from the Memorial Hermann Colorectal Liver Metastasis System Roadmap Draft v0.6 (4 October 2026, liver-directed section revised 3 October 2026, evidence current to 20 September 2026) and its companion guideline alignment worksheet of the same date, which supplied the institutional positions, the NCCN decisions 1-16 and the open local approval items. Revised on 7 October 2026 (Batch 08) after a full-text read of the whole CRLM reference depot: 45 papers, each with an independently recorded critique, covering all 45 PubMed-indexed references cited on this page. Every evidence string was re-checked against the paper's own reported results rather than against a guideline quoting it, and the grades were re-set where the full text showed the recommendation rested on a surrogate endpoint, a subset analysis, an unvalidated threshold or a single centre's practice; 20 evidence entries changed and 13 grades were lowered in that pass, and the limited-evidence section was rewritten and expanded from 5 entries to 27. Three references are cited only for what they do not yet show: the older PUMP protocol is now supplemented by the ASCO 2026 randomized abstract; the LIGRO survival analysis is published separately and was not read, so ALPPS is cited for resectability only; and the NCCN guideline, the OPTN policy and guidance documents, the Memorial Hermann roadmap and its alignment worksheet are not PubMed-indexed papers and were read as documents, not trials. Policy wording follows NCCN Colon Cancer v2.2026 (7 April 2026), OPTN Policy 9 as retrieved 1 October 2026, and the OPTN Adult MELD Exceptions for Transplant Oncology review-board guidance of December 2025, which is guidance and not Policy. The roadmap itself is a draft pending multidisciplinary and institutional governance review: it is not active clinical policy, does not replace clinician judgement, current drug labelling, OPTN policy or patient-specific informed consent, and every transplant criterion must be confirmed against current policy at implementation. HAI sections updated 15 October 2026 to Batch 09. New studies were checked against indexed abstracts and the published ASCO abstract; new full-text PDFs remain to be acquired. No new full-text review is claimed for these additions."
}

            "41990853",

          "l": "Standard",

   "questions": [
    {
     "id": "cHCC-CCA-R1",
     "set": "roadmap",
     "title": "Surgery or transplantation after nodal or extrahepatic disease",
     "question": "When combined HCC–cholangiocarcinoma has nodal or extrahepatic disease that responds, is resection or transplantation reasonable?",
     "kind": "clinical",
     "status": "Proposed; transplantation closed · OPEN proposal",
     "where": [],
     "proposal": "Resection with regional lymphadenectomy remains the curative option for organ-confined disease. After a response of regional nodal disease, decide case by case using the iCCA rules (iCCA-R1); distant extrahepatic disease stays systemic-therapy-led. Transplantation is closed after any nodal or extrahepatic disease, as in iCCA-B4.",
     "rules": [
      "Regional nodal disease that responds: MDT case-by-case resection with lymphadenectomy; confirm response by restaging and tissue where feasible.",
      "Distant extrahepatic disease: systemic therapy; no conversion pathway (no published data).",
      "Transplantation: previous nodal or extrahepatic disease excludes transplantation, as for iCCA (iCCA-B4)."
     ],
     "rationale": "In resected cHCC–CCA, nodal metastasis and local extrahepatic invasion carry large hazard ratios, and no study reports surgery after extrahepatic response. After transplantation, recurrence is frequent and mostly extrahepatic.",
     "studies": [
      {
       "source": "Jiang 2020 · resected cHCC-CC",
       "key": "ehd-chcca_jiang2020",
       "population": "Single-centre cohort, 55 resections; distant metastasis excluded. Nodal metastasis in 11 (20%).",
       "results": "Nodal metastasis: survival HR 6.95 (2.15–22.44); local extrahepatic invasion HR 4.91; 5-year survival 16.4% overall.",
       "limits": "Small; survival by nodal status shown only as curves and hazard ratios, without numeric rates.",
       "locator": "Gastroenterol Rep 2020; Tables 2–3.",
       "read": "Full text read"
      },
      {
       "source": "Kim 2023 · cHCC-CC LT, Korea",
       "key": "ehd-chcca_kim2023",
       "population": "Nine-centre cohort, 111 transplant recipients with cHCC–CC. Diagnosis on explant; nodal metastasis in 3.",
       "results": "Recurrence 44.1% vs 19.1% in HCC; first recurrence extrahepatic-only in 37 of 49.",
       "limits": "Nodal signal rests on 3 patients.",
       "locator": "World J Gastrointest Surg 2023; Results, Table 4.",
       "read": "Full text read"
      },
      {
       "source": "Dageforde 2020 · cHCC-CCA LT vs resection",
       "key": "ehd-chcca_dageforde2020",
       "population": "12-centre US cohort, 208 cHCC–CCA. Nodal and extrahepatic status not reported.",
       "results": "Beyond UCSF, 5-year survival 15.8%; within Milan, transplant survival similar to HCC.",
       "limits": "Diagnosis on final pathology; only 5.3% recognized as cHCC–CCA before surgery.",
       "locator": "J Am Coll Surg 2021; Results.",
       "read": "Full text read"
      },
      {
       "source": "Sierra 2026 · cHCC-CCA LT, UNOS",
       "key": "ehd-chcca_sierra2026",
       "population": "UNOS cohort, 309 candidates. No tumor-level variables.",
       "results": "Lowest 15-year survival among primary liver cancers (graft-loss HR 1.79; death HR 1.67).",
       "limits": "Registry coding; no nodal data.",
       "locator": "HPB 2026; Results.",
       "read": "Full text read"
      }
     ],
     "counter": "No direct study; regional nodal disease does not by itself prove futility, and nodal metastasis predicts death and recurrence (Jiang HR 6.95; Kim, 3 node-positive recipients), but no absolute survival rates by nodal status are reported.",
     "certainty": "Very low.",
     "change": "Any series of resection after response of nodal disease in cHCC–CCA.",
     "web": "chcca/#question-cHCC-CCA-R1"
    },
    {
     "id": "cHCC-CCA-D1",
     "set": "roadmap",
     "title": "Does this programme transplant for combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma, under whose governance, and against which written criteria?",
     "question": "Does this programme transplant for combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma, under whose governance, and against which written criteria?",
     "kind": "governance",
     "status": "OPEN — not yet decided",
     "where": [
      {
       "label": "5 · Assess transplant eligibility",
       "url": "chcca/#decision-5"
      }
     ],
     "positions": [
      {
       "source": "Dageforde 12-centre analysis",
       "key": "pm33316425",
       "says": "Within Milan, 67 recipients had 5-year survival of 70.1% versus 73.4% for HCC (p=0.806) but double the recurrence; roadmap critique: only 2 of 99 recipients were knowingly transplanted with the diagnosis, and Milan was assigned on imaging.",
       "locator": "Gate 5 · Reasonable 'Transplantation for cHCC-CCA within Milan criteria…' (pref, avoid); What we are not sure about · item 3"
      },
      {
       "source": "Kodali 2026 matched cohort",
       "key": "pm41685088",
       "says": "Nineteen incidentally diagnosed recipients carried mortality hazard ratios of 6.47 against controls matched before transplant and 4.67 against controls matched on explant pathology; nine died of metastatic adenocarcinoma.",
       "locator": "Gate 5 · Avoid 'Do not promise long-term graft and patient survival at HCC rates' (avoid); What we are not sure about · item 7"
      },
      {
       "source": "Lunsford 2018 propensity-matched series",
       "key": "pm29573187",
       "says": "Concluded that low-grade tumours should not be excluded; read in full, it shows non-significantly worse 5-year recurrence-free survival when matched on pre-transplant characteristics (42% versus 61%, p=0.17, in its results; 28% in its abstract).",
       "locator": "Gate 5 · Reasonable 'Differentiation grade and the explant pathological variables…' (note); What we are not sure about · items 7–8"
      },
      {
       "source": "Sierra 2026 UNOS analysis",
       "key": "pm42049568",
       "says": "Among 309 candidates, waitlist mortality and dropout were the lowest of three diagnoses, yet post-transplant survival was the worst: 27.3% at 15 years, adjusted HR 1.67 for death against HCC.",
       "locator": "Gate 5 · Avoid 'Do not promise long-term graft and patient survival at HCC rates' (pref, note); What we are not sure about · item 6"
      },
      {
       "source": "Kimura 2026 meta-analysis",
       "key": "pm42068695",
       "says": "Six retrospective studies give a pooled 5-year odds ratio of 0.55 favouring transplantation over resection; roadmap critique: smaller tumours in transplant arms, one matched study, unstable on leave-one-out, and the authors concede selection may explain it.",
       "locator": "Gate 5 · Reasonable 'Transplantation for cHCC-CCA within Milan criteria…' (note)"
      }
     ],

     "set": "roadmap",
     "title": "Liver treatment after extrahepatic disease responds",
     "question": "After extrahepatic HCC responds to systemic therapy or is treated locally, when should resection or ablation of the liver tumor be offered?",
     "kind": "clinical",
     "status": "Proposed; MDT selection · OPEN proposal",
     "where": [],
     "proposal": "Systemic therapy remains the standard for HCC with extrahepatic spread. After all sites respond or remain stable, the multidisciplinary team may consider liver resection or ablation for selected patients with localized spread if every residual site can be treated. The survival benefit of adding liver treatment is uncertain. See HCC-B5 for transplant eligibility.",
     "rules": [
      "Localized extrahepatic spread (JLCA 2023, BR1): a solitary node at station 3, 8 or 12; localized peritoneal disease (P1); a unilateral adrenal metastasis; or a few lung metastases. All other extrahepatic disease is BR2: benefit of surgery uncertain.",
      "Before surgery: response or stable disease of every extrahepatic site on serial imaging, no new lesions, current whole-body staging, every intrahepatic and extrahepatic site treatable (resection, ablation or stereotactic radiotherapy), adequate liver reserve, ECOG 0–1. No guideline sets the interval; the MDT records the interval it uses.",
      "AASLD 2023 does not support systemic therapy before resection outside trials. Record the decision as an MDT exception or enroll in a study or registry; plan continued systemic therapy and surveillance.",
      "Discuss recurrence even when all visible lesions are treated. In the 40-patient SABR trial, 2-year freedom from local progression was 91.1% and 2-year progression-free survival was 0%."
     ],
     "rationale": "The strongest direct evidence for liver surgery after response comes from selected observational cohorts. Studies treating metastases show that local control can be durable despite progression elsewhere. The Japanese consensus defines the limited patterns of spread for multidisciplinary review.",
     "studies": [
      {
       "source": "JLCA/JSHBPS 2023 resectability consensus (Akahoshi 2024)",
       "key": "ehd-hcc_jlca2023",
       "population": "Japanese expert consensus on oncological resectability (17 panelists). Statement 9 (15/17): extrahepatic spread is basically BR2; localized spread could be BR1 (solitary node at station 3, 8 or 12; P1 peritoneum; unilateral adrenal; few lung metastases).",
       "results": "Cites 5-year survival of 29.5% after resection of node-positive HCC and 27–66% after lung metastasectomy.",
       "limits": "Surgeon-only panel; a classification, not a treatment recommendation; permissive (“could be”); no response or interval criteria.",
       "locator": "Liver Cancer 2024; Statement 9 and summary.",
       "read": "Full text read"
      },
      {
       "source": "Zhang 2024 · surgery after response with EHD",
       "key": "ehd-hcc_zhang2024",
       "population": "15-centre cohort, 150 patients with extrahepatic metastases whose intrahepatic tumor reached partial or complete response (mRECIST). Only 8 of 26 operated patients had their metastases removed; 85% had partial (not complete) response of extrahepatic disease.",
       "results": "Median survival 16.5 vs 11.3 months from response (surgery vs none); progression-free survival not different.",
       "limits": "Immortal-time bias; operated patients more often oligometastatic; counts inconsistent.",
       "locator": "Sci Rep 2024; Results.",
       "read": "Full text read"
      },
      {
       "source": "Choi 2026 · NCDB curative treatment after ICI",
       "key": "ehd-hcc_choi2025",
       "population": "US national cancer database, 4,329 patients on first-line immunotherapy. 138 (3.2%) had curative treatment afterwards, including 15 with distant and 10 with nodal metastasis.",
       "results": "Propensity-matched HR for death after curative treatment was 0.22 (0.14–0.33) in the Results section (IPTW 0.20). The abstract reports 0.20 and 0.19, respectively. These are observational estimates.",
       "limits": "Immortal-time bias; curative intent uncertain; modality not separated for the 15 distant and 10 nodal patients.",
       "locator": "Liver Cancer. 2026;15(2):193–204. Tables 1–3, pp. 196–200.",
       "read": "Full text read"

       "source": "Hasegawa 2014 · node-positive HCC, Japanese survey",
       "key": "ehd-hcc_hasegawa2014",
       "population": "Japanese national survey, 14,872 resections. 112 with pathologically proven nodal metastasis.",
       "results": "3-year survival 38.9% (nodal) vs 27.2% (distant stage IVB).",
       "limits": "Pre-immunotherapy era; surgeon-selected patients.",
       "locator": "Ann Surg. 2014;259:166–170. Survival by nodal status, pp. 166–168 and Figure 1.",
       "read": "Full text read"
      },
      {
       "source": "Midorikawa 2020 · resection of extrahepatic recurrence",
       "key": "ehd-hcc_midorikawa2020",
       "population": "Single-center retrospective cohort of 64 patients with resectable extrahepatic recurrence after liver resection. Intrahepatic disease was absent or controlled. Of 64 eligible patients, 38 had metastasectomy and 26 received other treatment.",
       "results": "Median overall survival after treatment for extrahepatic recurrence was 5.3 years with metastasectomy and 1.1 years with other treatment.",
       "limits": "Patients selected for surgery were younger and had a longer disease-free interval. Median follow-up was 1.2 years. Five-year survival after surgery differs between the abstract (60.5%) and Results (55.9%); both give 9.1% for other treatment.",
       "locator": "Hepatol Res. 2020;50:978–984. Selection pp. 979–980, survival pp. 978 and 981, Fig. 2B p. 982.",
       "read": "Full text read"

       "source": "Choi 2024 · SABR for oligometastatic HCC, phase II",
       "key": "ehd-hcc_choi2024",
       "population": "Prospective, single-arm phase II trial. Forty patients received stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) to 62 metastases.        "results": "At 2 years, freedom from local progression was 91.1%, overall survival 80% and progression-free survival 0%. Median progression-free survival was 5.3 months from SABR.",
       "limits": "Median follow-up was 15.5 months. Systemic therapy was permitted. The single-arm design cannot establish a survival benefit from SABR.",

       "results": "Unadjusted 2-year freedom from local progression per lesion was 98.2% with surgery vs 97.0% with SBRT. Unadjusted two-year overall survival was 74.0% versus 57.6% (P=.006).      "title": "Surgery after oligometastatic disease responds",

     "kind": "clinical",
     "status": "Proposed; trial or registry first · OPEN proposal",
     "where": [],
     "proposal": "Distant metastasis stays systemic-therapy-led. Response-selected conversion surgery for limited liver metastases is offered preferably within a trial (METAPANC, CSPAC-1) or a registry after MDT review. Metachronous isolated lung metastases after a long disease-free interval may be resected. There is no PDAC transplant pathway.",
     "rules": [
      "Synchronous liver oligometastases: ≤3 liver metastases (OligoPanc working definition, relative-majority only; METAPANC ≤3 liver-only), no peritoneal or other extrahepatic disease, induction chemotherapy without progression (METAPANC: 8 cycles of mFOLFIRINOX; Heidelberg: usually ≥6 cycles with RECIST response of metastases and a marker fall), CA19-9 fall >50% to <500 U/mL (CSPAC-1), resectable primary and metastases.",
      "Counsel: in Heidelberg, 46% were unresectable at exploration and only about 1 in 4 explored was ypM0; median survival 25.5 months (ypM0) vs 10.7 (ypM1) vs 8.1 (exploration only). Surgery ≥9 months after diagnosis did worse.",
      "Metachronous isolated lung metastases: ≤3 (ideally solitary), unilateral, disease-free interval of about 2 years (17–28 months cited), after systemic therapy and MDT review.",
      "Para-aortic (16b1) nodes known before surgery are systemic disease and outside the OligoPanc Delphi definition (although panellists rated a para-aortic nodal vignette as oligometastatic); when found at operation, do not abort resection on 16b1 alone."

     "rationale": "Survival after resection is concentrated in complete responders, and unselected resection of metastases does not help. Trial rules give the clearest selection thresholds.",

       "limits": "Expert opinion.",
       "locator": "Lancet Oncol 2026; Results.",
       "read": "Full text read"
      },

files.old: {"1309988":{"kind":"case-series","limitations":["No limitations section; the authors concede only that the results depend entirely on obtaining histologically free resection margins, that extensive preoperative and perioperative assessment is needed so that inappropriate extensive resection is avoided, that prospective studies of preoperative biliary drainage in obstructive jaundice have failed to show significant overall benefit although they still use it in selected cases, and that published results of transplantation for this disease have generally been poor with a high incidence of recurrence"],"critique":["Twenty-three resections accumulated over thirty years at one centre, during which imaging, staging and operative technique changed completely; the type-specific operative recommendations rest on one to four patients per tumour type, and the type IV recommendation of transplantation on three patients, one of whom recurred in the hepatic pedicle 8 months after transplantation","No statistical comparison of any kind appears in the paper: no P value, no log-rank test and no confidence interval, so the claim that group C outcomes exceeded groups A and B is purely descriptive","Three different counts are given for the same set of potentially curative resections: 7 patients with two type I lesions in the abstract, 8 patients with three type I lesions in the Results and Discussion, and 9 patients in group C in Table 2","The 70-year-old patient with a papillary tumour who survived 11 years free of recurrence was removed from the survival analysis as atypical after her outcome was known, while remaining the case that supports the abstract's recommendation of local excision for type I disease; she is 71 in Table 1 and 70 in the text","The claim that local recurrence was never observed when the margin was histologically free is contradicted by the paper's own Table 1 and Results, where two group C patients died of recurrence at 14 and 22 months, one of them with recurrence at the anastomosis and in the hepatic pedicle at 10 months","Operative mortality is reported as zero with mortality defined as death during or within two months of surgery, a window wider than the conventional 30 or 90 days; zero events in 23 patients carries an upper confidence bound near 15%","There is no comparison group: patients treated by surgical bypass or transtumoral intubation were never analysed, only 23 of 122 operated patients were resected, and the survival credited to margin-negative resection is uncontrolled and heavily selected","Group B is defined as microscopic tumour at the resection margin or lymph nodes outside the hepatic pedicle, so margin status and nodal status are mixed in one group and the margin effect is not isolated","Figure 1, showing operative type IV rising from 4 to 9 on postoperative histology, includes the 3 transplanted patients and so counts 26 cases, while the survival analysis excludes them and counts 23, so classification accuracy and outcome are computed on different denominators","Follow-up averaged 26 months with a minimum of 6, and 10 patients were still alive at 6 to 48 months, so the 3-year figures of 25% overall survival and 50% in group C rest on almost no patients still at risk, with no numbers at risk given anywhere","Caudate resection was performed in only 8 of the 13 liver resections, yet the recommendation is that every type II to IV lesion requires it; that recommendation rests on Nimura's anatomical argument rather than on any comparison within this series","Table 3's assessment of curability excludes the 4 patients with gross residual tumour and 3 with distant nodal disease, leaving 16 patients from whom the entire type-specific operative algorithm is derived","Ten of the 23 patients (43%) had already undergone surgical drainage or transtumoral intubation elsewhere and all but 5 had been investigated or treated at another institution, so this is a referred, pre-treated population","Preoperative percutaneous drainage is endorsed for selected cases while the paper itself cites two prospective studies showing no benefit, and only one patient in the series actually received it","Denominators shift between the 136 consecutive patients, the 122 taken to surgery and the 23 resected, with the 19% resectability rate and the 15.6% and 7.4% curative resection rates all computed on 122","No chemotherapy, radiotherapy or adjuvant treatment data are reported for any patient, and causes of death are not tabulated","No linked editorial or comment was found in PubMed"],"n":"23 resections for hilar cholangiocarcinoma performed between January 1960 and December 1990 at one Paris centre, drawn from 136 consecutive patients of whom 122 were considered suitable for surgical treatment, with 3 further patients treated by total hepatectomy and transplantation excluded from the outcome analysis","bottom_line":"This is the source of the modified Bismuth-Corlette classification and of the type-driven operation: local excision for type I, with caudate resection added for type II, with right or left hepatectomy for type III, and transplantation considered for type IV. It rests on 23 resections over thirty years at one centre, one to four patients per type, no comparison group, no statistical test of any kind, and a classification the paper itself shows is unreliable before operation, four operative type IV lesions becoming nine on histology. What it establishes is that margin clearance rather than nodal status drove outcome in this series and that achieving it requires the hepatectomy the anatomy dictates; the survival figures and the type IV recommendation should not be carried forward.","funding":"No funding statement and no declaration of interests anywhere in the paper"},"16135931":{"kind":"cohort","limitations":["No limitations section; the authors state 'We acknowledge difficulties in comparing results between the resection and transplant groups' and then set out the selection asymmetry: the transplant group was significantly younger with higher rates of primary sclerosing cholangitis and inflammatory bowel disease, by protocol design no transplant recipient had regional nodal metastases, medical selection criteria were more stringent for transplantation while tumour selection criteria were less stringent, and none of the transplant patients was a candidate for resection","Rosen concedes in the published discussion that the age difference between the groups is difficult to correct for, and that removing the patients with sclerosing cholangitis only partly corrects for it","Eight of the 38 recipients had no histological or cytological confirmation of carcinoma before neoadjuvant therapy; the authors note that one might be sceptical of those diagnoses and report that omitting them changes 5-year survival from 82% to 80%","The change in the timing of staging laparotomy in 2002, from near the time of transplantation to immediately after brachytherapy, may lower the yield of staging and allow disease progression to go undetected, leading to more recurrence after transplantation, which the authors state as an explicit concern","The most serious disadvantage of the protocol is the limitation of donor organ availability","The appealed MELD score of 20 was, in Rosen's own words in the discussion, an arbitrary decision agreed locally with the only other liver programme in the organ procurement organisation, and neither the correct starting point nor the correct increment is known","Transplantation becomes technically more difficult the longer a patient waits after neoadjuvant therapy and staging, with portal vein stenosis and friable tissues attributed to the radiation"],"critique":["The two survival curves start at different points. The 82% figure is survival from transplantation among the 38 who survived neoadjuvant therapy, staging and the waiting list, while 33 of the 71 enrolled never reached transplantation; the 21% figure is survival from operation among the 26 of 54 resected. From the start of treatment the comparison is 58% against about 21%, and Figure 1 is the only near-intention-to-treat comparison the paper offers","The best-selected resection subgroup did worse, not better: the node-negative margin-negative resections had 5-year survival of 18% against 21% for the whole resection group, which undercuts the argument that nodal and margin selection explains the gap","No statistical adjustment of any kind is attempted. The comparison is a log-rank test on unmatched groups differing by 15 years of mean age, by aetiology (22 of 38 transplant recipients had primary sclerosing cholangitis against 2 of 26 resections) and by protocol-mandated nodal status","Protocol exclusions make the groups non-exchangeable by construction: prior attempted resection or operative biopsy of the tumour barred a patient from the transplant arm, so patients who had been explored are structurally in the resection group","Five of the 71 protocol patients (7%) died during neoadjuvant therapy, four of sepsis and one of pulmonary embolism, and four more progressed beyond transplant criteria; none of this treatment-related mortality appears in the post-transplant curve that carries the paper's claim","Internal inconsistencies are not reconciled: the Results state that 8 of the 16 explants without residual tumour had unequivocal preoperative confirmation while the Discussion states 9 and refers to 'the other 7'; the node-negative margin-negative resection group is 15 patients in the Results and 16 in the Discussion and Figure 4; and 5-year survival after resection is 21% in the abstract and 20% in the Discussion","Sixteen of 38 explants (42%) contained no residual tumour, and from 2003 a CA 19-9 above 100 or digital image analysis or FISH aneuploidy alone sufficed for enrolment, so some transplanted patients may never have had cancer; Roberts raised exactly this point in the published discussion","Recurrence is compared as crude percentages, 13% against 27%, and mean time to recurrence as 40 against 21 months, although the transplant group's clock starts later and the follow-up durations of the two groups are never compared","At censoring one patient awaited staging and nine awaited transplantation; all are inside the 71-patient denominator of the intention-to-treat curve with minimal follow-up, and no numbers at risk appear on any figure","The comparator operation is not maximal by the paper's own standards: left hepatectomy in 13 of 26, extended right hepatectomy in only 1, and caudate resection in only 10 of 26 (38%), against the Neuhaus series quoted in the Discussion reporting 72% 5-year survival after margin-negative right trisegmentectomy with portal vein resection","Thirty-day mortality after resection was 12% (3 of 26), and Wall observes in the discussion that recurrence after resection was only about 30% while 5-year survival was 20%, implying that non-cancer deaths drive much of the difference","Seven living donor grafts were used and two of the three surgical deaths in the transplant arm followed living donor transplantation, yet no donor morbidity or mortality is reported and the organ cost of 38 grafts for 71 enrolled patients is never discussed","Twenty-three percent of patients taken to staging had findings precluding transplantation, but that yield is not stable across the study: before 2002 staging was done near the time of transplantation and nearly 40% of early patients had positive findings, while after the 2002 change very few did, so the single 23% figure spans two different practices","The CA 19-9 diagnostic criterion is reported in ng/mL rather than U/mL throughout","The published discussion (Ann Surg 2005;242:458-61) records the substantive objections: Roberts on diagnostic certainty in primary sclerosing cholangitis and on explant pathology, Shaw on the limited selection and the radiation dose, Wall on non-cancer mortality in the resected group, and Jenkins on how to counsel a non-PSC patient when the transplant results are set against resection results that every centre achieves","No linked editorial or comment was found in PubMed"],"n":"71 patients with unresectable hilar cholangiocarcinoma or cholangiocarcinoma arising in primary sclerosing cholangitis enrolled in the Mayo neoadjuvant chemoradiation and transplant protocol between January 1993 and August 2004, of whom 38 were transplanted, compared with 54 patients explored for potentially curative resection over the same period, of whom 26 were resected","bottom_line":"This is the Mayo single-centre report that put neoadjuvant chemoradiation followed by transplantation on the map, with 82% 5-year survival after transplantation against 21% after resection. The two figures are not comparable: by protocol no transplant patient was resectable and every recipient was proved node-negative at staging laparotomy, while 31% of resections were node-positive and 12% margin-positive, and the transplant curve starts at transplantation although 33 of 71 enrolled patients never got there, so from the start of treatment the comparison is 58% against about 21%. The defensible claim is what the protocol achieves in a selected, node-negative, mostly PSC population, in which 16 of 38 explants held no residual tumour and 8 recipients had no tissue proof of cancer.","funding":"No funding statement and no declaration of interests anywhere in the paper or the published discussion"},"21492336":{"kind":"cohort","limitations":["A primary weakness is that the groups were not randomised, although the authors state there were no remarkable demographic differences between them","The study is limited by its retrospective nature, and the authors judge that a prospective randomised trial comparing transperitoneal fine-needle aspiration with other diagnostic methods is unlikely to be feasible because the diagnosis is infrequent and patients ineligible for curative therapy may die before peritoneal seeding becomes clinically evident","The overall number of patients undergoing transperitoneal fine-needle aspiration is small, with six in the biopsy-positive group","Information such as tumour differentiation or perineural invasion was not known at enrolment given the limited amount of diagnostic tissue, so the groups could not be matched on the histological features that predict peritoneal spread","The reason the incidence of peritoneal seeding here exceeds that reported after percutaneous cholangiography and after fine-needle aspiration for hepatocellular carcinoma is unknown; the explanations offered, greater peritoneal exposure and relative immunosuppression after chemoradiotherapy, are hypotheses, and the authors note the second is unlikely because the biopsies preceded neoadjuvant therapy by weeks to months"],"critique":["The exposed group is six patients and the 83% figure rests on five events, so no precise risk estimate is possible; the interval around 5 of 6 runs from roughly a third to 100%","Reverse causation is not excluded. A transperitoneal aspiration that yields adenocarcinoma marks a tumour bulky and cell-rich enough to hit with a needle, and the finding that none of the nine aspiration-negative patients had peritoneal disease fits tumour biology at least as well as needle seeding","The patient with an equivocal biopsy showing glandular cells, who also had peritoneal metastasis demonstrated at staging, was set aside from the aspiration-positive group; with him the rate is 6 of 7, and the decision to exclude him is an adjudication made with the outcome already known","Table 2's footnote gives P = 0.0001 for the same comparison the abstract and Results report as P = 0.0097","The Discussion gives the no-biopsy group's metastasis rate as 20% overall with 11% peritoneal, where the Results and Table 2 give 8% (14 of 175); five-year survival is 73% in the text and figure and 74% in the abstract","Table 2's denominators of 175, 6 and 9 sum to 190, not the 191 enrolled","The groups are declared similar with P = NS on 6 and 9 patients against 175, where no test could detect a difference; a mass was present in 16% of the aspiration-positive, 36% of the no-biopsy and 66% of the aspiration-negative patients, mean mass size was 3.9 against 2.9 cm, mean age 57 against 50 years, and primary sclerosing cholangitis 17% against 40%","Brush cytology was not performed at all in the aspiration-positive group, so the comparison is between patients diagnosed by needle and patients diagnosed endoscopically, that is between two diagnostic pathways rather than two exposures","Every aspiration was performed at an outside facility, so needle gauge, number of passes, operator and technique are uncontrolled, and 13 percutaneous and 3 EUS-guided procedures are pooled despite differing peritoneal exposure; how many of the three EUS procedures were positive is never stated","Only patients already accepted onto the transplant protocol are counted, so anyone whose outside aspiration took them out of transplant consideration never enters the denominator, and the result cannot be extended to patients being worked up for resection","The interval from aspiration to staging is never reported, only the interval from enrolment to staging, and two patients were staged before enrolment, noted only in a table footnote","No time-to-event analysis and no adjustment for calendar era is attempted across an 18-year span in which protocol criteria, cross-sectional imaging and EUS availability all changed","The 73% five-year survival is reported for the 125 transplanted patients with numbers at risk falling to 33 by five years, and no intention-to-treat figure is given for the 191 enrolled, 66 of whom never reached transplantation","The benchmark used for comparison, a 2.7% needle-track seeding rate after biopsy of hepatocellular carcinoma, is a different endpoint from peritoneal carcinomatosis found at staging laparotomy","No linked editorial or comment was found in PubMed"],"n":"191 patients with localised unresectable hilar cholangiocarcinoma enrolled in the Mayo neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and liver transplant protocol between 1 October 1992 and 1 January 2010, of whom 16 had undergone transperitoneal fine-needle aspiration of the primary tumour at an outside facility (13 percutaneous, 3 EUS-guided) and 125 reached transplantation","bottom_line":"This is the paper behind the rule that a hilar mass must not be sampled transperitoneally in anyone who might be a transplant candidate: 5 of 6 protocol patients with a positive outside fine-needle aspiration had peritoneal metastases at operative staging, against 8% of the 175 who had no aspiration. The exposed group is six patients and five events, the comparison is retrospective and unmatched on the histological features that predict peritoneal spread, and a needle that yields adenocarcinoma marks a tumour bulky enough to hit, so reverse causation is not excluded. It also records the Mayo protocol's eligibility rules more explicitly than any other paper in this set, including that pathological confirmation is not required to proceed.","funding":"No funding statement; conflict of interests declared as none"},"22504095":{"kind":"cohort","limitations":["The study was not a randomised controlled trial, and the authors argue that a trial of transplantation with or without neoadjuvant therapy would be extremely difficult given the rarity of the disease and the unacceptably high recurrence historically reported after transplantation alone","A large proportion of patients came from one centre, 193 of 287, creating a potential for bias, which the authors address by showing no statistical difference in intent-to-treat or recurrence-free survival between that centre and the other 11","Heterogeneity in the duration, type and dose of maintenance chemotherapy across centres meant the independent impact of maintenance chemotherapy could not be determined","Pretransplant surgical staging failed to show a statistical advantage in recurrence-free survival, which the authors attribute mostly to lack of power given that only 30 transplanted resist neoadjuvant therapy","Patients without a visible mass on cross-sectional imaging were counted as having a mass smaller than 3 cm for statistical purposes, which the authors state was necessary files.new: {"1309988":{"kind":"case-series","limitations":["No limitations section; the authors concede only that the results depend entirely on obtaining histologically free resection margins, that extensive preoperative and perioperative assessment is needed so that inappropriate extensive resection is avoided, that prospective studies of preoperative biliary drainage in obstructive jaundice have failed to show significant overall benefit although they still use it in selected cases, and that published results of transplantation for this disease have generally been poor with a high incidence of recurrence"],"critique":["Twenty-three resections accumulated over thirty years at one centre, during which imaging, staging and operative technique changed completely; the type-specific operative recommendations rest on one to four patients per tumour type, and the type IV recommendation of transplantation on three patients, one of whom recurred in the hepatic pedicle 8 months after transplantation","No statistical comparison of any kind appears in the paper: no P value, no log-rank test and no confidence interval, so the claim that group C outcomes exceeded groups A and B is purely descriptive","Three different counts are given for the same set of potentially curative resections: 7 patients with two type I lesions in the abstract, 8 patients with three type I lesions in the Results and Discussion, and 9 patients in group C in Table 2","The 70-year-old patient with a papillary tumour who survived 11 years free of recurrence was removed from the survival analysis as atypical after her outcome was known, while remaining the case that supports the abstract's recommendation of local excision for type I disease; Three limits of that read should be named rather than implied. First, one reference is effectively abstract-level: in Gillmeister 2026 (PMID 42698384, a brief report) the Results section did not survive text extraction, so every figure quoted from it comes from its Table 1, abstract and Discussion and is expressed per biopsy rather than per patient, and its patient count, malignancy prevalence and PSC subgroup size could not be read. Revised on 7 October 2026 (Batch 08) after a full-text read of this page's reference depot. All 39 PubMed-indexed references were read in full and abstracted with an independent critique: 19 from the perihilar cholangiocarcinoma depot and 20 shared papers drawn from the intrahepatic CCA depot, which supplies the biliary systemic-therapy trials (ABC-02, TOPAZ-1, KEYNOTE-966, ABC-06, BILCAP, BCAT, PRODIGE-12, ASCOT), the targeted-therapy trials (ClarIDHy, FIGHT-202, FOENIX-CCA2, ROAR, HERIZON-BTC-01), the hepatic arterial infusion trial, the AASLD, BSG, ESMO 2023 and ESMO 2024 interim guidelines, and the two next-generation sequencing studies from the developing centre. Three limits of that read should be named rather than implied. First, one reference is effectively abstract-level: in Gillmeister 2026 (PMID 42698384, a brief report) the Results section did not survive text extraction, so every figure quoted from it comes from its Table 1, abstract and Discussion and is expressed per biopsy rather than per patient, and its patient count, malignancy prevalence and PSC subgroup size could not be read. Second, several linked editorials and correspondence were identified in PubMed but not obtained in full, so no critique point on this page is attributed to them: Alipour's editorial on Bardhi 2025 (PMID 40518235), Bridgewater, Webster and Amin's comment on the DRAINAGE trial (PMID 30122357), the four ABC-06 correspondence letters, and the paywalled Lancet Oncology comments on ClarIDHy, where the cost-of-benefit point is reported second-hand and should be treated as provisional. Third, SWOG S0809 was first cited as quoted by BSG 2023; its primary report (Ben-Josef, J Clin Oncol 2015, PMID 25964250) was read in full on 29 October 2026, and the non-PubMed sources — NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v1.2026, OPTN Policy 9, the OPTN review-board guidance, the UTHealth protocol v2, the HOPE4LIVER one-year update, the roadmap itself and its alignment worksheet — were read as documents but not abstracted or critiqued in the same way. Where a figure in the earlier draft could not be traced to any of these sources it has been replaced with one that can, and the removals are visible in the text: the reported incidence split for IDH1 between intrahepatic and extrahepatic disease, and a per-site adjuvant hazard ratio for hilar tumours, are both gone. Built from the Memorial Hermann Perihilar Cholangiocarcinoma System Roadmap, Draft v0.6, dated 4 October 2026 (with the liver-directed treatment revision of 3 October 2026), and its companion Guideline alignment worksheet of the same version and date, which compares AASLD 2023, BSG 2023, the ESMO 2024 interim update, the Asia-Pacific 2024 consensus, OPTN policy and review-board guidance, and NCCN Biliary Tract Cancers v1.2026 (10 March 2026) across sixteen areas. The decision points follow the roadmap's own sequence: §2 (its clinical decision 0, drainage), §3 (define the extent), §4 and §4.1 (tissue and route), §5 (its clinical decision 1, resectable disease), §6 (its clinical decision 2, the transplant protocol), and §7 (its Decision points 3 and 4). Allocation criteria are from OPTN Policy 9.5.A and 9.4.C–E, official PDF checked 1 October 2026, with the programme's own standard perihilar CCA protocol v2 (policy review 16 July 2026). Perihilar cholangiocarcinoma is included in the shared liver-directed therapy matrix. The matrix link provides the current cross-disease comparison. This revision changed grades as well as numbers. Forty-five evidence strings were rewritten and twenty-seven of them were regraded downward where the full-text critique did not support the grade assigned from study design, and the reason is given in each string's note; the page now carries one grade-A string where it previously carried seven. No recommendation was removed: the roadmap's positions stand, and the page's job is to say how well supported each one is. This page reproduces a draft pending multidisciplinary and institutional governance review: it is not active clinical policy, it does not replace clinician judgement, and every numeric criterion must be verified against the current source before use." }

files.old: { "key": "incidental", "short": "Incidental", "name": "Incidental liver mass", "version": "v0.2", "batch": "Batch 08, 7 October 2026", "lead": "Characterize the liver lesion, decide whether further testing is needed, and select the appropriate disease-specific treatment pathway.", "gatelabel": "Clinical decisions", "gates": [ { "id": "0", "tone": "loco", "name": "0 · Assess background liver disease", "req": "any", "crit": [ "Cirrhosis of any aetiology", "Chronic hepatitis B infection, with or without cirrhosis", "Current or prior hepatocellular carcinoma, including a liver transplant candidate or recipient", "None of the above — a liver with no risk factor for primary liver cancer", "A vascular liver disorder, congenital hepatic fibrosis, or age under 18 — a separate category in which LI-RADS does not apply at all" ], "ask": "Does the patient have a liver disease or risk factor that permits a noninvasive HCC diagnosis?", "standard": [ { "t": "Answer the at-risk question first, because it decides which diagnostic criteria you are permitted to use for the rest of the workup.", "l": "Standard", "g": "B", "refs": [ "30251931", "39690085", "37199193" ], "pref": "Every incidental liver lesion, before the next scan is ordered. The LI-RADS at-risk population is cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis B, and current or prior HCC including adult transplant candidates. AASLD 2023 and EASL 2025 both build their diagnostic algorithms on that same population and both use the LI-RADS lexicon; EASL 2025 states that LI-RADS should be preferred over its own 2018 algorithm because of the LR-M and LR-TIV categories, while noting the two perform similarly for HCC (LoE 3, strong recommendation).", "avoid": "Do not let the referral's wording settle this. 'Known liver disease' on a request form is not the same as cirrhosis, and MASLD without cirrhosis is not an at-risk liver under either guideline.", "note": "Record the aetiology and how cirrhosis was established — histology, imaging, elastography, platelet count, or clinical decompensation. The at-risk answer is the single most consequential line in the report." }, { "t": "In an at-risk liver, categorise the observation with CT/MRI LI-RADS v2018 and put the category in the report — but read the category as a probability derived from retrospective high-prevalence cohorts, not as a measurement.", "l": "Standard", "g": "C", "refs": [ "30251931", "30445016", "34783596", "39690085" ], "pref": "Every observation in an at-risk liver. In a systematic review of 17 retrospective studies, 2,760 patients and 3,556 observations, the pooled proportions confirmed as HCC and as any malignancy were 94% (95% CI 92-96) and 97% (95-99) for LR-5, 74% (67-80) and 80% (75-85) for LR-4, 38% (31-45) and 40% (31-50) for LR-3, 13% (8-22) and 14% (9-21) for LR-2, and 36% (26-48) and 93% (87-97) for LR-M; no malignancy was found in LR-1.", "avoid": "Three things undercut those figures. All 17 studies were retrospective and observation selection was the commonest high-risk domain, through verification bias and case-control design, so the LR-3 and LR-4 figures are probably inflated relative to an unselected incidental population; the authors themselves call the LR-2 estimate provisional and at high risk of bias while still recommending that LR-2 management be reconsidered, and this page does not inherit that recommendation. The 2022 individual-patient-data meta-analysis of 5,364 observations from 32 studies then shows the major features are not equivalent: nonperipheral washout carried an odds ratio of 13.2 (95% CI 9.0-19.2) and nonrim arterial hyperenhancement 10.3 (6.7-15.6), enhancing capsule only 2.4 (1.7-3.5), and threshold growth was not associated with HCC at all, OR 1.6 (0.8-3.4) — a result the same paper reports a second time as 1.6 (0.7-3.6), p=0.07.", "note": "The agreement figures matter as much as the probabilities. Interreader agreement for arterial hyperenhancement and washout is excellent, kappa 0.84-0.87, but agreement on the category that actually drives management is fair for CEUS (kappa 0.30-0.39), fair to substantial for MRI (0.35-0.61) and substantial for CT (0.79), and intermodality agreement is kappa 0.33-0.39 between CT and MRI and 0.22 between MRI and CEUS. A category is not a stable property of the lesion. See the quick reference for the v2018 table." }, { "t": "In a liver that is not at risk, accept that no imaging criterion set exists that can call a lesion hepatocellular carcinoma — EASL 2025 says so explicitly, and the consequence is that an unresolved solid lesion here needs tissue, not another category.", "l": "Standard", "g": "B", "refs": [ "39690085" ], "pref": "The young patient, the patient with no liver disease, and the patient with MASLD and no cirrhosis. EASL 2025: the non-invasive criteria should only be applied to patients with cirrhosis, chronic HBV infection or a history of HCC, and in other patients the diagnosis of HCC should be confirmed by biopsy (LoE 1, strong recommendation). The guideline gives its own reason — the pre-test probability in these populations has not been precisely established.", "avoid": "Do not apply a LI-RADS category outside the at-risk population and then act on it. The number means nothing there, and it will be read as though it did.", "note": "This does not mean every solid lesion in a normal liver needs a needle. Most are haemangioma, focal fat or focal nodular hyperplasia and are resolved on this page at decision points 4 and 5. It means that an unresolved solid lesion in a normal liver cannot be declared malignant or benign by imaging category alone." } ], "alt": [ { "t": "Where cirrhosis is suspected but not established, say so in those words and treat the pathway as undetermined rather than guessing in either direction.", "l": "Reasonable", "g": "D", "pref": "Advanced fibrosis on elastography without decompensation, a nodular liver contour without portal hypertension, long-standing alcohol use with normal synthetic function. Name the uncertainty, get the hepatology opinion, and decide the pathway once.", "avoid": "Do not default to the at-risk pathway because it feels safer. It is not neutral: it licenses a treat-without-tissue decision for LR-5, and in a non-cirrhotic liver that decision has no evidence behind it." }, { "t": "In a liver with a vascular disorder — Budd-Chiari, chronic portal vein occlusion, obliterative portal venopathy, hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia, cardiac congestion — treat the case as its own category and get it to a benign-liver-tumour multidisciplinary review rather than through either arm of this assessment.", "l": "Reasonable", "g": "D", "refs": [ "26516032", "30251931", "42191146" ], "pref": "These livers generate multiple arterially hyperenhancing benign nodules — in Budd-Chiari syndrome, imaging displays hepatic nodules in 60-80% of patients, usually under 4 cm, frequently more than ten, hypervascular and disseminated, with no pathognomonic CT or MRI pattern — and LI-RADS specifically excludes cirrhosis caused by vascular disorders and by congenital hepatic fibrosis from its population. EASL's vascular-liver-disease guideline is the document that governs them, and it states plainly that characterisation of these nodules cannot rely on the HCC criteria validated in cirrhosis.", "avoid": "Do not categorise a hyperenhancing nodule in a Budd-Chiari liver as LR-4 or LR-5 and act on it, and do not treat benignity as settled either: cumulative HCC incidence in Budd-Chiari syndrome is about 4% at a median 5 years. Note what the guideline does not give you — it reports how often these nodules occur in patients known to have vascular disease, and never the inverse probability a radiologist actually faces, which is the chance of underlying vascular disease given multiple hypervascular nodules in a non-cirrhotic liver. The five biopsy triggers it suggests (three or fewer nodules, a nodule 3 cm or larger, heterogeneity or venous-phase washout, change across two studies, rising alpha-fetoprotein) come from one cited source with no sensitivity or specificity, in the same paragraph that says the only formal recommendation is multidisciplinary surveillance.", "note": "Two provenance warnings. First, the EASL vascular-liver guidance this page quotes is the 2015 document, built on the agenda of a single 2012 conference with a PubMed-only search and committee opinion where evidence was absent; it has been superseded by a 2026 EASL edition that this page has not obtained, so every statement sourced to it here is provisional and must be re-checked against the new edition before clinical use.             approval requirements that every high-risk view also shows.
Nothing here changes clinical content: every field is copied from those sources.

import json, re
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import quote

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
BASE = '/mh-liver-pathways/'
DATE = '1 November 2026'
C = json.loads((ROOT / 'transplant/assets/content.json').read_text())
EHD = json.loads((ROOT / 'tools/ehd_positions.json').read_text())
HQ = json.loads((ROOT / 'tools/consensus_source/high_risk_questions.json').read_text())
HR = C['high_risk']
HRSRC = HR['sources']
STEPS = {(p['slug'], st['id']): st['title'] for p in C['index'] for st in p['steps']}
STATUS = dict(re.findall(r"'([a-z0-9-]+)':\['(?:closed|mixed|review|research|open|study|safety|checklist|limited)','([^']+)'\]",
                         (ROOT / 'transplant/assets/high-risk.js').read_text()))

TUMORS = [
    dict(key='hcc', code='HCC', name='Hepatocellular carcinoma', roadmap='hcc', transplant='hcc'),
    dict(key='pcca', code='pCCA', name='Perihilar cholangiocarcinoma', roadmap='hilar', transplant='pcca'),
    dict(key='icca', code='iCCA', name='Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma', roadmap='icca', transplant='icca'),
    dict(key='crlm', code='CRLM', name='Colorectal liver metastases', roadmap='crlm', transplant='crlm'),
    dict(key='nelm', code='NELM', name='Neuroendocrine liver metastases', roadmap='nelm', transplant='nelm'),
    dict(key='hehe', code='HEHE', name='Hepatic epithelioid hemangioendothelioma', roadmap=None, transplant='hehe'),
    dict(key='hca', code='HCA', name='Hepatocellular adenoma', roadmap='adenoma', transplant='hca'),
    dict(key='chcca', code='cHCC-CCA', name='Combined hepatocellular–cholangiocarcinoma', roadmap='chcca', transplant=None),
    dict(key='pdac', code='PDAC', name='Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma', roadmap='pdac', transplant=None),
    dict(key='pnet', code='pNET', name='Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor', roadmap='pnet', transplant=None),
    dict(key='ampullary', code='AMP', name='Ampullary tumors', roadmap='ampullary', transplant=None),
    dict(key='pcyst', code='PCYST', name='Pancreatic cysts', roadmap='pcyst', transplant=None),
    dict(key='incidental', code='INC', name='Incidental liver lesions', roadmap='incidental', transplant=None),
]
HR_LABEL = {'hehe': 'High-risk pathway (boundary addendum)', 'hca': 'High-risk pathway (boundary addendum)'}
# Extrahepatic-disease questions and not-applicable notes, by tumor key.
EHD_TUMOR = {'HCC': 'hcc', 'cHCC–CCA': 'chcca', 'iCCA': 'icca', 'pCCA': 'pcca', 'CRLM': 'crlm', 'NELM': 'nelm', 'pNET': 'pnet',
             'HEHE': 'hehe', 'PDAC': 'pdac', 'Ampullary': 'ampullary'}
EHD_NA = {'Hepatocellular adenoma': 'hca', 'Pancreatic cystic lesions': 'pcyst', 'Incidental liver lesions': 'incidental'}


def files(t):
    """Standardized file names (identical on the website and in the V17 package)."""
    c = t['code'].replace('-', '')
    f = {}
    if t['roadmap']:
        f['roadmap_info'] = f'{c}_1_Roadmap.docx'
        f['roadmap_questions'] = f'{c}_2_Roadmap_Questions.docx'
    if t['transplant']:
        f['standard_info'] = f'{c}_3_Standard_Pathway.docx'
        f['standard_questions'] = f'{c}_4_Standard_Pathway_Questions.docx'
        f['highrisk_info'] = f'{c}_5_High_Risk_Pathway.docx'
        f['highrisk_questions'] = f'{c}_6_High_Risk_Pathway_Questions.docx'
    f['decision'] = f'{c}_7_Decision_Discussion.docx'
    return f


def links_for(pmid='', doi='', url='', tmc='', pmc=''):
    L = {}
    if pmid: L['pubmed'] = f'https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/{pmid}/'
    if doi: L['doi'] = 'https://doi.org/' + doi
    if pmc: L['pmc'] = pmc
    if url and url not in L.values(): L['url'] = url
    if tmc: L['tmc'] = tmc
    elif doi: L['tmc'] = 'https://libkey.io/libraries/480/' + doi
    return L


class Sources:
    def __init__(self): self.s = {}
    def add(self, key, short, title='', kind='', **links):
        if key and key not in self.s: self.s[key] = dict(short=short, title=title, kind=kind, links={k: v for k, v in links.items() if v})
        return key


def gate_names(slug):
    if slug == 'hcc':
        return dict(re.findall(r'\{id:"([^"]+)", tone:"[a-z]+", name:"([^"]+)"', (ROOT / 'hcc/index.html').read_text()))
    return {g['id']: g['name'] for g in json.loads((ROOT / f'{slug}/data/pathway.json').read_text())['gates']}


GATES = {t['roadmap']: gate_names(t['roadmap']) for t in TUMORS if t['roadmap']}


def roadmap_refs(slug):
    if slug == 'hcc':
        return {}, {}
    d = json.loads((ROOT / slug / 'data/pathway.json').read_text())
    return d['refs'], d['nonpm']


def roadmap_set(t, S):
    slug = t['roadmap']
    src = json.loads((ROOT / f'tools/consensus_source/roadmap_{slug}.json').read_text())
    refs, nonpm = roadmap_refs(slug)
    out = []
    # Extrahepatic-disease question for this roadmap first: it is the newest open position.
    for q in EHD['questions']:
        if q['setting'] == 'roadmap' and EHD_TUMOR.get(q['tumor']) == t['key']:
            out.append(ehd_question(q, S, 'roadmap', f'{slug}/#question-{q["id"]}'))
    for q in src['questions']:
        positions = []
        for p in q.get('positions', []):
            ref = str(p.get('ref') or '')
            key = None
            if ref in refs:
                r = refs[ref]; key = S.add('pm' + ref, r[0], r[2], r[1], **links_for(pmid=ref))
            elif ref in nonpm:
                r = nonpm[ref]; key = S.add('np-' + slug + '-' + ref, r[0], r[2], r[1], **links_for(url=r[3] if len(r) > 3 else ''))
            elif re.fullmatch(r'\d{6,9}', ref):
                key = S.add('pm' + ref, p['source'], '', '', **links_for(pmid=ref))
            positions.append(dict(source=p['source'], key=key, says=p['position'], locator=p.get('locator', '')))
        out.append(dict(id=q['id'], set='roadmap', title=q['question'], question=q['question'], kind=q['kind'],
                        status='OPEN — not yet decided', where=[dict(label=GATES[slug].get(str(d), f'Decision {d}'), url=f'{slug}/#decision-{d}') for d in q.get('decisions', [])],
                        positions=positions, divergence=q.get('divergence', ''), proposal=q.get('proposal', ''),
                        proposal_locator=q.get('proposal_locator', ''), rationale=q.get('rationale', ''), audit=q.get('audit', ''),
                        web=f'{slug}/#question-{q["id"]}'))
    ratify = [dict(id=r['id'], specialty=r['specialty'], question=r['question'], kind=r.get('kind', ''), proposal=r.get('proposal', ''),
                   proposal_locator=r.get('proposal_locator', ''),
                   positions=[dict(source=p['source'], key=None, says=p['position'], locator=p.get('locator', '')) for p in r.get('positions', [])])
              for r in src.get('ratify', [])]
    if t['key'] == 'pdac':
        for qid in ('PDAC-B1', 'PDAC-B2'):
            out.append(pdac_question(qid, S))
    return out, ratify


def pdac_question(qid, S):
    r = HQ[qid]; ps = HQ['_pdac_sources']
    for k, v in ps.items():
        S.add('hr-' + k, v['short'], v['title'], 'Study or consensus', **links_for(pmid=v.get('pmid', ''), doi=v.get('doi', ''), url=v.get('url', '')))
    return dict(id=qid, set='roadmap', title=r['question'], question=r['question'], kind='transplant (no PDAC transplant pathway)',
                status='OPEN — not activated; no PDAC transplant route', where=[], positions=positions_from_records(r['source_positions'], S),
                proposal=r['stance'] or '', rules=r['rules'] or [], rationale=r['rationale'] or '', tests=r['tests'] or '', allocation=r['allocation'] or '',
                owners=r['owner'] or '', note=r['roadmap'] or '', supporting=[ps[k]['short'] for k in r.get('supporting_refs', []) if k in ps],
                web='pdac/#question-' + qid)


def hr_source(key, S):
    s = HRSRC.get(key) or HQ['_pdac_sources'].get(key)
    if not s:
        return None
    pdf = next((x['url'] for x in s.get('pdf_links', []) if 'pmc.ncbi' in x.get('url', '')), '')
    return S.add('hr-' + key, s['short'], s.get('title', ''), 'Study, guidance or policy',
                 **links_for(pmid=s.get('pmid') or '', doi=s.get('doi') or '', url=s.get('url', ''), tmc=s.get('tmc', ''), pmc=pdf))


def positions_from_records(evidence, S):
    out = []
    for e in evidence or []:
        k = hr_source(e.get('key'), S)
        short = S.s[k]['short'] if k else e.get('key', '')
        out.append(dict(source=short, key=k, says=(('“' + e['quote'] + '”') if e.get('quote') else '') + (' ' + e['meaning'] if e.get('meaning') else ''),
                        locator=e.get('locator', '')))
    return out


def studies(review, S):
    out = []
    for s in review['evidence'].get('studies', []):
        k = hr_source(s.get('key'), S)
        out.append(dict(source=S.s[k]['short'] if k else s.get('key', ''), key=k, population=' '.join(x for x in [s.get('design_population', ''), s.get('selection', '')] if x),
                        results=s.get('results', ''), limits=s.get('limits', ''), locator=s.get('locator', '')))
    return out


def ehd_question(q, S, setting, web):
    rows = []
    for s in q['evidence']:
        src = EHD['sources'][s['key']]
        k = S.add('ehd-' + s['key'], src['short'], '', 'Study, guidance or policy', **src.get('links', {}))
        rows.append(dict(source=src['short'], key=k, population=(s['design_population'] + ' ' + s['selection']).strip(), results=s['results'],
                         limits=s['limits'], locator=s['locator'], read={'full': 'Full text read', 'abstract': 'Abstract only; full text pending'}.get(s['read'], '')))
    return dict(id=q['id'], set=setting, title=q['title'], question=q['question'], kind='clinical', status=q['status'] + ' · OPEN proposal',
                where=[], proposal=q['position'], rules=q['rules'], rationale=q['why'], studies=rows, counter=q['counter'],
                certainty=q['certainty'], change=q['change'], web=web)


def standard_set(t, S):
    p = next(x for x in C['index'] if x['slug'] == t['transplant'])
    out = []
    for i in p['issues']:
        pos = []
        for c in i['comparisons']:
            s = C['sources'][c['ref']]
            k = S.add('std-' + c['ref'], s['short'], s.get('title', ''), s.get('kind', ''), **links_for(url=s.get('url', '')))
            pos.append(dict(source=s['short'], key=k, kind=s.get('kind', ''), says=('“' + c['text'] + '”') if c['quote'] else c['text'],
                            locator=c.get('locator') or s.get('locator', '')))
        rid = i['record'].replace(' — detailed web subquestion', ' (detail)')
        steps = [s for s in p['steps'] if i['id'] in s.get('issues', [])]
        out.append(dict(id=rid, set='standard', title=i['question'], question=i['question'], kind='standard pathway', status=i['status'],
                        where=[dict(label=s['title'], url=f'transplant/{p["slug"]}/#{s["id"]}') for s in steps],
                        positions=pos, proposal=i['proposal'], rationale=i['rationale'], owners=i.get('owners', ''),
                        web=f'transplant/{p["slug"]}/#meeting-{i["id"]}'))
    return out


def review_question(r, slug, S, shared=False):
    rec = HQ.get(r['id'], {})
    ehd = next((q for q in EHD['questions'] if q['id'] == r['id']), None)
    question = rec.get('question') or (ehd['question'] if ehd else r['title'])
    ev = r['evidence']
    return dict(id=r['id'], set='highrisk', title=r['title'], question=question, kind='shared approval requirement' if shared else 'high-risk review',
                status=STATUS.get(r['anchor'], 'OPEN proposal') + ' · not activated', context=r.get('context', ''),
                where=[dict(label=STEPS.get((slug, s), s), url=f'transplant/{slug}/#{s}') for s in (r.get('steps') or []) if isinstance(s, str)],
                positions=positions_from_records(rec.get('source_positions'), S), proposal=r.get('stance', ''), rules=r.get('rules', []),
                tests=r.get('tests', ''), allocation=r.get('allocation', ''), rationale=ev.get('synthesis', ''), counter=ev.get('counterevidence', ''),
                certainty=ev.get('certainty', ''), threshold_basis=ev.get('threshold_basis', []), studies=studies(r, S),
                web=f'transplant/{slug}/#high-risk-{r["anchor"]}')


def highrisk_set(t, S):
    slug = t['transplant']
    qs = [review_question(r, slug, S) for r in HR['pathways'][slug]['reviews']]
    shared = [review_question(r, slug, S, True) for r in HR['readiness']]
    return qs, shared


manifest = {'generated': DATE, 'base': 'documents/', 'tumors': {}}
for t in TUMORS:
    S = Sources()
    sets = {}
    if t['roadmap']:
        qs, ratify = roadmap_set(t, S)
        sets['roadmap'] = dict(label='Roadmap', page=t['roadmap'] + '/', web=t['roadmap'] + '/#questions', questions=qs, ratify=ratify)
    if t['transplant']:
        sets['standard'] = dict(label='Standard pathway', page=f'transplant/{t["transplant"]}/', web=f'transplant/{t["transplant"]}/#meeting',
                                questions=standard_set(t, S))
        qs, shared = highrisk_set(t, S)
        sets['highrisk'] = dict(label=HR_LABEL.get(t['key'], 'High-risk pathway'), page=f'transplant/{t["transplant"]}/#high-risk',
                                web=f'transplant/{t["transplant"]}/#high-risk', questions=qs, shared=shared)
    na = [dict(id='EHD-' + t['code'], text=n['position']) for n in EHD['not_applicable'] if EHD_NA.get(n['tumor']) == t['key']]
    doc = dict(key=t['key'], code=t['code'], name=t['name'], generated=DATE, files=files(t), sets=sets, not_applicable=na, sources=S.s)
    out = ROOT / 'documents' / t['key']
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (out / 'questions.json').write_text(json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + '\n')
    manifest['tumors'][t['key']] = dict(code=t['code'], name=t['name'], roadmap=t['roadmap'], transplant=t['transplant'],
                                        files=files(t), counts={k: len(v['questions']) for k, v in sets.items()})
    print(f"{t['code']:9} " + ' · '.join(f'{k} {len(v["questions"])}' for k, v in sets.items()) + f' · {len(S.s)} sources')
(ROOT / 'assets/documents.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + '\n')

    if pmid: L['pubmed'] = f'https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/{pmid}/'
    if doi: L['doi'] = 'https://doi.org/' + doi
    if pmc: L['pmc'] = pmc
    if url and url not in L.values(): L['url'] = url
    if tmc: L['tmc'] = tmc
    elif doi: L['tmc'] = 'https://libkey.io/libraries/480/' + doi
    return L


class Sources:
    def __init__(self): self.s = {}
    def add(self, key, short, title='', kind='', **links):
        if key and key not in self.s: self.s[key] = dict(short=short, title=title, kind=kind, links={k: v for k, v in links.items() if v})
        return key


def gate_names(slug):
    if slug == 'hcc':
        return dict(re.findall(r'\{id:"([^"]+)", tone:"[a-z]+", name:"([^"]+)"', (ROOT / 'hcc/index.html').read_text()))
    return {g['id']: g['name'] for g in json.loads((ROOT / f'{slug}/data/pathway.json').read_text())['gates']}


GATES = {t['roadmap']: gate_names(t['roadmap']) for t in TUMORS if t['roadmap']}


def roadmap_refs(slug):
    if slug == 'hcc':
        return {}, {}
    d = json.loads((ROOT / slug / 'data/pathway.json').read_text())
    return d['refs'], d['nonpm']


def roadmap_set(t, S):
    slug = t['roadmap']
    src = json.loads((ROOT / f'tools/consensus_source/roadmap_{slug}.json').read_text())
    refs, nonpm = roadmap_refs(slug)
    out = []
    # Extrahepatic-disease question for this roadmap first: it is the newest open position.
    for q in EHD['questions']:
        if q['setting'] == 'roadmap' and EHD_TUMOR.get(q['tumor']) == t['key']:
            out.append(ehd_question(q, S, 'roadmap', f'{slug}/#question-{q["id"]}'))
    for q in src['questions']:
        positions = []
        for p in q.get('positions', []):
            ref = str(p.get('ref') or '')
            key = None
            if ref in refs:
                r = refs[ref]; key = S.add('pm' + ref, r[0], r[2], r[1], **links_for(pmid=ref))
            elif ref in nonpm:
                r = nonpm[ref]; key = S.add('np-' + slug + '-' + ref, r[0], r[2], r[1], **links_for(url=r[3] if len(r) > 3 else ''))
            elif re.fullmatch(r'\d{6,9}', ref):
                key = S.add('pm' + ref, p['source'], '', '', **links_for(pmid=ref))
            positions.append(dict(source=p['source'], key=key, says=p['position'], locator=p.get('locator', '')))
        out.append(dict(id=q['id'], set='roadmap', title=q['question'], question=q['question'], kind=q['kind'],
                        status=q.get('status', 'OPEN — not yet decided'), resolved=q.get('resolved', False), where=[dict(label=GATES[slug].get(str(d), f'Decision {d}'), url=f'{slug}/#decision-{d}') for d in q.get('decisions', [])],
                        positions=positions, divergence=q.get('divergence', ''), proposal=q.get('proposal', ''),
                        proposal_locator=q.get('proposal_locator', ''), rationale=q.get('rationale', ''), audit=q.get('audit', ''),
                        web=f'{slug}/#question-{q["id"]}'))
    ratify = [dict(id=r['id'], specialty=r['specialty'], question=r['question'], kind=r.get('kind', ''), proposal=r.get('proposal', ''),
                   proposal_locator=r.get('proposal_locator', ''),
                   positions=[dict(source=p['source'], key=None, says=p['position'], locator=p.get('locator', '')) for p in r.get('positions', [])])
              for r in src.get('ratify', [])]
    if t['key'] == 'pdac':
        for qid in ('PDAC-B1', 'PDAC-B2'):
            out.append(pdac_question(qid, S))
    return out, ratify


def pdac_question(qid, S):
    r = HQ[qid]; ps = HQ['_pdac_sources']
    for k, v in ps.items():
        S.add('hr-' + k, v['short'], v['title'], 'Study or consensus', **links_for(pmid=v.get('pmid', ''), doi=v.get('doi', ''), url=v.get('url', '')))
    return dict(id=qid, set='roadmap', title=r['question'], question=r['question'], kind='transplant (no PDAC transplant pathway)',
                status='OPEN — not activated; no PDAC transplant route', where=[], positions=positions_from_records(r['source_positions'], S),
                proposal=r['stance'] or '', rules=r['rules'] or [], rationale=r['rationale'] or '', tests=r['tests'] or '', allocation=r['allocation'] or '',
                owners=r['owner'] or '', note=r['roadmap'] or '', supporting=[ps[k]['short'] for k in r.get('supporting_refs', []) if k in ps],
                web='pdac/#question-' + qid)


def hr_source(key, S):
    s = HRSRC.get(key) or HQ['_pdac_sources'].get(key)
    if not s:
        return None
    pdf = next((x['url'] for x in s.get('pdf_links', []) if 'pmc.ncbi' in x.get('url', '')), '')
    return S.add('hr-' + key, s['short'], s.get('title', ''), 'Study, guidance or policy',
                 **links_for(pmid=s.get('pmid') or '', doi=s.get('doi') or '', url=s.get('url', ''), tmc=s.get('tmc', ''), pmc=pdf))


def positions_from_records(evidence, S):
    out = []
    for e in evidence or []:
        k = hr_source(e.get('key'), S)
        short = S.s[k]['short'] if k else e.get('key', '')
        out.append(dict(source=short, key=k, says=(('“' + e['quote'] + '”') if e.get('quote') else '') + (' ' + e['meaning'] if e.get('meaning') else ''),
                        locator=e.get('locator', '')))
    return out


def studies(review, S):
    out = []
    for s in review['evidence'].get('studies', []):
        k = hr_source(s.get('key'), S)
        out.append(dict(source=S.s[k]['short'] if k else s.get('key', ''), key=k, population=' '.join(x for x in [s.get('design_population', ''), s.get('selection', '')] if x),
                        results=s.get('results', ''), limits=s.get('limits', ''), locator=s.get('locator', '')))
    return out


def ehd_question(q, S, setting, web):
    rows = []
    for s in q['evidence']:
        src = EHD['sources'][s['key']]
        k = S.add('ehd-' + s['key'], src['short'], '', 'Study, guidance or policy', **src.get('links', {}))
        rows.append(dict(source=src['short'], key=k, population=(s['design_population'] + ' ' + s['selection']).strip(), results=s['results'],
                         limits=s['limits'], locator=s['locator'], read={'full': 'Full text read', 'abstract': 'Abstract only; full text pending'}.get(s['read'], '')))
    return dict(id=q['id'], set=setting, title=q['title'], question=q['question'], kind='clinical', status=q['status'] + ' · OPEN proposal',
                where=[], proposal=q['position'], rules=q['rules'], rationale=q['why'], studies=rows, counter=q['counter'],
                certainty=q['certainty'], change=q['change'], web=web)


def standard_set(t, S):
    p = next(x for x in C['index'] if x['slug'] == t['transplant'])
    out = []
    for i in p['issues']:
        pos = []
        for c in i['comparisons']:
            s = C['sources'][c['ref']]
            k = S.add('std-' + c['ref'], s['short'], s.get('title', ''), s.get('kind', ''), **links_for(url=s.get('url', '')))
            pos.append(dict(source=s['short'], key=k, kind=s.get('kind', ''), says=('“' + c['text'] + '”') if c['quote'] else c['text'],
                            locator=c.get('locator') or s.get('locator', '')))
        rid = i['record'].replace(' — detailed web subquestion', ' (detail)')
        steps = [s for s in p['steps'] if i['id'] in s.get('issues', [])]
        out.append(dict(id=rid, set='standard', title=i['question'], question=i['question'], kind='standard pathway', status=i['status'], resolved=i.get('resolved', False),
                        where=[dict(label=s['title'], url=f'transplant/{p["slug"]}/#{s["id"]}') for s in steps],
                        positions=pos, proposal=i['proposal'], rationale=i['rationale'], owners=i.get('owners', ''),
                        web=f'transplant/{p["slug"]}/#meeting-{i["id"]}'))
    return out


def review_question(r, slug, S, shared=False):
    rec = HQ.get(r['id'], {})
    ehd = next((q for q in EHD['questions'] if q['id'] == r['id']), None)
    question = rec.get('question') or (ehd['question'] if ehd else r['title'])
    ev = r['evidence']
    return dict(id=r['id'], set='highrisk', title=r['title'], question=question, kind='shared approval requirement' if shared else 'high-risk review',
                status=STATUS.get(r['anchor'], 'OPEN proposal') + ' · not activated', context=r.get('context', ''),
                where=[dict(label=STEPS.get((slug, s), s), url=f'transplant/{slug}/#{s}') for s in (r.get('steps') or []) if isinstance(s, str)],
                positions=positions_from_records(rec.get('source_positions'), S), proposal=r.get('stance', ''), rules=r.get('rules', []),
                tests=r.get('tests', ''), allocation=r.get('allocation', ''), rationale=ev.get('synthesis', ''), counter=ev.get('counterevidence', ''),
                certainty=ev.get('certainty', ''), threshold_basis=ev.get('threshold_basis', []), studies=studies(r, S),
                web=f'transplant/{slug}/#high-risk-{r["anchor"]}')


def highrisk_set(t, S):
    slug = t['transplant']
    qs = [review_question(r, slug, S) for r in HR['pathways'][slug]['reviews']]
    shared = [review_question(r, slug, S, True) for r in HR['readiness']]
    return qs, shared


manifest = {'generated': DATE, 'base': 'documents/', 'tumors': {}}
for t in TUMORS:
    S = Sources()
    sets = {}
    if t['roadmap']:
