        "CLARINET establishes that lanreotide 120 mg delays radiographic progression in somatostatin-receptor-positive, grade 1 or 2 enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, with a hazard ratio of 0.47 (95% CI 0.30–0.73) and 65.1% versus 33.0% progression-free at 24 months, and it does so across hepatic tumour volumes above and below 25%. What it does not establish is that this changes anything a patient feels or how long they live: no statistically significant difference in overall survival or quality of life was demonstrated, the population was non-functioning and 96% radiographically stable at entry, and subgroup estimates do not establish a predictive grade threshold; grade 2 HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22–0.91). The placebo arm ran a median 18.0 months without progression, which is the figure to carry into any discussion of whether to start treatment now or watch, and the hepatic-volume subgroup everyone quotes was collapsed from five prespecified categories to two after the data were in.",
        "The subgroup that matters most for liver-directed decisions is a post hoc construction. Hepatic tumour volume was prespecified in five categories whose estimated hazard ratios ranged from 0.24 to 0.54, and was collapsed after the fact into a dichotomy at 25%. The conclusion that the effect holds irrespective of hepatic tumour volume rests on that simplification, as the paper's own table footnote states.",
        "CLARINET’s grade 2 subgroup HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22–0.91). The HR 0.58 (0.32–1.04) belongs to the pancreatic-primary subgroup. Subgroup estimates do not establish differential benefit by grade or primary site.",
        "CLARINET subgroup estimates are exploratory: the pancreatic subgroup HR was 0.58 (95% CI 0.32–1.04), hepatic tumour volume >25% HR 0.45 (0.23–0.88), and grade 2 HR 0.45 (0.22–0.91). These are different strata. The estimates do not establish a predictive primary-site, grade or liver-volume cutoff.",
        "The whole benefit is radiographic. Overall survival did not differ, EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status did not differ, and the population was non-functioning by design so there were no hormonal symptoms to improve. Crossover is invoked to explain the survival null without any crossover numbers or a sensitivity analysis being presented.",
        "The size of the effect is unknown because the trial ended before it could be measured. Median progression-free survival was not reached with lanreotide within the 96-week fixed study duration, so the delay is known only to exceed the observation window, and the 96-week design cannot address how long treatment should continue.",
        "Progression-free survival and time to tumour progression return the identical 18.0-month placebo median from different event counts (60 against 58), which shows the median sits in a sparse region of the curve where two events make no difference to the estimate.",
        "The chromogranin A result is reported on 64 of 101 and 64 of 103 patients, roughly two-thirds of each arm, with no account of the missing third, and it is a biochemical change in a non-functioning tumour population where it carries no symptomatic meaning.",
        "Enrolment required somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy uptake of grade 2 or higher within the previous 6 months, so the trial selected the patients most likely to respond and says nothing about receptor-poor disease, which is precisely the group in whom embolisation, chemotherapy or resection is being weighed.",
        "The trial excluded any prior radionuclide therapy at any time, chemoembolisation or chemotherapy within 6 months, and more than 15 days of previous somatostatin analogue. The cohort is therefore essentially naive to liver-directed treatment, and nothing in the result informs sequencing with embolisation, radioembolisation or PRRT.",
        "The discussion raises the obvious reading of its own data, that an 18-month placebo median supports watchful waiting, and sets it aside on the ground that the study examined prevention of progression. That is a restatement of the trial's design, not an answer to the question of whether delaying treatment costs the patient anything.",
        "The adverse events that matter for a surgical population are presented as reassurance. Cholelithiasis occurred in 10% against 3% and hyperglycaemia in 5% against 0%, and the serious treatment-related events in the lanreotide arm include biliary fistula and cholelithiasis, in patients who may later need hepatectomy or arterial therapy; the discussion calls the safety profile favourable by comparison with targeted agents and chemotherapy.",
        "The sponsor controlled the trial end to end. Ipsen, which markets lanreotide, designed, funded and conducted the study; the contract research organisation's statisticians worked under the oversight of the sponsor's own biostatistics department; a medical writer paid by the sponsor drafted the manuscript; and one co-author is affiliated to Ipsen.",
        "Two letters in the New England Journal of Medicine with an author reply are linked to this paper in PubMed (PMIDs 25317882, 25317883 and 25317881). The full texts could not be obtained, so no point above draws on them and whatever objections they raise are not represented here.",
        "Start a somatostatin analogue for antiproliferative effect and symptom control.",
        "Standard",
        "A",
        "Receptor-positive or functional phenotypes, and anyone in whom progression would be hard to salvage. PROMID (n=85, treatment-naive midgut) gave time to progression 14.3 versus 6.0 months, hazard ratio 0.34 (95% CI 0.20–0.59); CLARINET (n=204, non-functioning enteropancreatic, Ki-67 under 10%) gave a progression-free survival hazard ratio of 0.47 (0.30–0.73) with 24-month progression-free survival 65.1% versus 33.0%.",
        "Do not make it mandatory for every patient. Grade A applies to the antiproliferative indication in unresectable disease: PROMID and CLARINET enrolled only patients with no curative option, unresectable disease or declined surgery. In resectable or ablatable disease, analogue versus resection or ablation is an MDT decision.",
        "Neither trial established an overall-survival benefit — CLARINET found no significant difference in overall survival or quality of life, and PROMID is an interim analysis at 67 progressions and 16 deaths of a trial that enrolled 85 of a planned 162 patients and was then closed for slow accrual, so its confirmatory survival analysis at 121 deaths was never performed. The effect is stabilisation, not shrinkage: one partial remission per arm in PROMID, and objective remissions with an analogue are rare. For a liver pathway the decisive limitation is that PROMID's exploratory burden subgroups had imprecise estimates and did not establish a predictive liver-volume threshold — hazard ratio 0.17 (0.08–0.40) at 0 to 10% hepatic involvement, 0.40 (0.10–1.67) at 10 to 50% and 0.71 (0.11–4.45) above 50%, with 95% of patients having Ki-67 of 2% or less and 64/85 (75%) having 10% or less liver involvement, including those without liver disease. CLARINET held across hepatic volume, hazard ratio 0.45 (0.23–0.88) above 25%, but that dichotomy is a post hoc simplification of a prespecified five-category variable whose component hazard ratios ran 0.24 to 0.54. For carcinoid-syndrome control the source is ENETS 2024, not these trials.",
        "Continue the somatostatin analogue for functional-syndrome control where it is needed, and after clinically significant progression in a nonfunctional tumour do not automatically continue it for antiproliferative benefit.",
        "C",
        "Functional disease, where the analogue is doing hormonal work that nothing else in the plan replaces.",
        "Carrying an analogue indefinitely in a nonfunctional tumour that has progressed on it, on the assumption that it is still holding the tumour back.",
        "Downgraded to C: this is a position taken in the absence of evidence rather than from it. The NANETS midgut panel reached no consensus on continuing an analogue past progression, and no trial has tested continuation after documented progression in either direction — PROMID and CLARINET both enrolled patients who were not progressing, 96% of CLARINET patients having had no progression in the 3 to 6 months before randomisation. The roadmap's position is that the indication after progression is hormonal, not antiproliferative; that is a defensible reading of what the trials enrolled, not a demonstrated equivalence.",
        "Do not continue a somatostatin analogue for antiproliferative benefit in every nonfunctional NET after significant progression.",
        "Avoid",
        "B",
        "Continue it for hormonal control where the tumour is functional.",
        "PROMID and CLARINET tested delay of progression in stable, indolent disease — 96% of CLARINET patients had no progression in the 3 to 6 months before randomisation — and neither establishes an antiproliferative role after documented progression.",
        "Octreotide LAR or lanreotide",
        "PROMID: time to progression 14.3 versus 6 months with octreotide versus placebo in midgut NET. CLARINET established PFS benefit with lanreotide in nonfunctional enteropancreatic NET, Ki-67 <10%.",
        "CLARINET randomized double-blind trial, 204 nonfunctioning advanced enteropancreatic NET patients (101 lanreotide, 103 placebo).",
        "From randomization, median PFS not reached with lanreotide versus 18 months placebo; HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.30–0.73). Twenty-four-month PFS 65.1% versus 33.0%. No significant OS or QoL difference in the primary report. Diarrhea 26% versus 9%.",
        "Shows that stability and substantial survival without LT are plausible; does not estimate the added benefit of transplant or support treating all stable low-burden NET. G2 up to 20% and G3 are not represented by this <10% trial threshold."

    "25014687": {
      "label": "CLARINET",
      "design": "RCT",
      "arms": "Lanreotide vs placebo",
      "result": "Primary endpoint met: median PFS not reached vs 18.0 mo (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73); 24-mo PFS 65.1% vs 33.0%; no OS or QoL difference",
      "caution": "96% stable; grade 2 HR 0.45 (0.22–0.91), pancreatic HR 0.58 (0.32–1.04); no predictive cutoff",
      "quotes": [
        "204 patients with unresectable or metastatic, somatostatin-receptor-positive, grade 1 or 2 (Ki-67 under 10%) non-functioning enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours randomised at 48 centres in 14 countries between June 2006 and April 2013: 101 to lanreotide Autogel 120 mg and 103 to placebo, with 96% having had no documented progression in the preceding 3 to 6 months.",
        "CLARINET establishes that lanreotide 120 mg delays radiographic progression in somatostatin-receptor-positive, grade 1 or 2 enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, with a hazard ratio of 0.47 (95% CI 0.30–0.73) and 65.1% versus 33.0% progression-free at 24 months, and it does so across hepatic tumour volumes above and below 25%. What it does not establish is that this changes anything a patient feels or how long they live: no statistically significant difference in overall survival or quality of life was demonstrated, the population was non-functioning and 96% radiographically stable at entry, and subgroup estimates do not establish a predictive grade threshold; grade 2 HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22–0.91). The placebo arm ran a median 18.0 months without progression, which is the figure to carry into any discussion of whether to start treatment now or watch, and the hepatic-volume subgroup everyone quotes was collapsed from five prespecified categories to two after the data were in.",
        "The subgroup that matters most for liver-directed decisions is a post hoc construction. Hepatic tumour volume was prespecified in five categories whose estimated hazard ratios ranged from 0.24 to 0.54, and was collapsed after the fact into a dichotomy at 25%. The conclusion that the effect holds irrespective of hepatic tumour volume rests on that simplification, as the paper's own table footnote states.",
        "CLARINET’s grade 2 subgroup HR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22–0.91). The HR 0.58 (0.32–1.04) belongs to the pancreatic-primary subgroup. Subgroup estimates do not establish differential benefit by grade or primary site.",
        "CLARINET subgroup estimates are exploratory: the pancreatic subgroup HR was 0.58 (95% CI 0.32–1.04), hepatic tumour volume >25% HR 0.45 (0.23–0.88), and grade 2 HR 0.45 (0.22–0.91). These are different strata. The estimates do not establish a predictive primary-site, grade or liver-volume cutoff.",
        "The whole benefit is radiographic. Overall survival did not differ, EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status did not differ, and the population was non-functioning by design so there were no hormonal symptoms to improve. Crossover is invoked to explain the survival null without any crossover numbers or a sensitivity analysis being presented.",
        "The size of the effect is unknown because the trial ended before it could be measured. Median progression-free survival was not reached with lanreotide within the 96-week fixed study duration, so the delay is known only to exceed the observation window, and the 96-week design cannot address how long treatment should continue.",
        "Progression-free survival and time to tumour progression return the identical 18.0-month placebo median from different event counts (60 against 58), which shows the median sits in a sparse region of the curve where two events make no difference to the estimate.",
        "The chromogranin A result is reported on 64 of 101 and 64 of 103 patients, roughly two-thirds of each arm, with no account of the missing third, and it is a biochemical change in a non-functioning tumour population where it carries no symptomatic meaning.",
        "Enrolment required somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy uptake of grade 2 or higher within the previous 6 months, so the trial selected the patients most likely to respond and says nothing about receptor-poor disease, which is precisely the group in whom embolisation, chemotherapy or resection is being weighed.",
        "The trial excluded any prior radionuclide therapy at any time, chemoembolisation or chemotherapy within 6 months, and more than 15 days of previous somatostatin analogue. The cohort is therefore essentially naive to liver-directed treatment, and nothing in the result informs sequencing with embolisation, radioembolisation or PRRT.",
        "The discussion raises the obvious reading of its own data, that an 18-month placebo median supports watchful waiting, and sets it aside on the ground that the study examined prevention of progression. That is a restatement of the trial's design, not an answer to the question of whether delaying treatment costs the patient anything.",
        "The adverse events that matter for a surgical population are presented as reassurance. Cholelithiasis occurred in 10% against 3% and hyperglycaemia in 5% against 0%, and the serious treatment-related events in the lanreotide arm include biliary fistula and cholelithiasis, in patients who may later need hepatectomy or arterial therapy; the discussion calls the safety profile favourable by comparison with targeted agents and chemotherapy.",
        "The sponsor controlled the trial end to end. Ipsen, which markets lanreotide, designed, funded and conducted the study; the contract research organisation's statisticians worked under the oversight of the sponsor's own biostatistics department; a medical writer paid by the sponsor drafted the manuscript; and one co-author is affiliated to Ipsen.",
        "Two letters in the New England Journal of Medicine with an author reply are linked to this paper in PubMed (PMIDs 25317882, 25317883 and 25317881). The full texts could not be obtained, so no point above draws on them and whatever objections they raise are not represented here.",
        "Start a somatostatin analogue for antiproliferative effect and symptom control.",
        "Standard",
        "A",
        "Receptor-positive or functional phenotypes, and anyone in whom progression would be hard to salvage. PROMID (n=85, treatment-naive midgut) gave time to progression 14.3 versus 6.0 months, hazard ratio 0.34 (95% CI 0.20–0.59); CLARINET (n=204, non-functioning enteropancreatic, Ki-67 under 10%) gave a progression-free survival hazard ratio of 0.47 (0.30–0.73) with 24-month progression-free survival 65.1% versus 33.0%.",
        "Do not make it mandatory for every patient. Grade A applies to the antiproliferative indication in unresectable disease: PROMID and CLARINET enrolled only patients with no curative option, unresectable disease or declined surgery. In resectable or ablatable disease, analogue versus resection or ablation is an MDT decision.",
        "Neither trial established an overall-survival benefit — CLARINET found no significant difference in overall survival or quality of life, and PROMID is an interim analysis at 67 progressions and 16 deaths of a trial that enrolled 85 of a planned 162 patients and was then closed for slow accrual, so its confirmatory survival analysis at 121 deaths was never performed. The effect is stabilisation, not shrinkage: one partial remission per arm in PROMID, and objective remissions with an analogue are rare. For a liver pathway the decisive limitation is that PROMID's exploratory burden subgroups had imprecise estimates and did not establish a predictive liver-volume threshold — hazard ratio 0.17 (0.08–0.40) at 0 to 10% hepatic involvement, 0.40 (0.10–1.67) at 10 to 50% and 0.71 (0.11–4.45) above 50%, with 95% of patients having Ki-67 of 2% or less and 64/85 (75%) having 10% or less liver involvement, including those without liver disease. CLARINET held across hepatic volume, hazard ratio 0.45 (0.23–0.88) above 25%, but that dichotomy is a post hoc simplification of a prespecified five-category variable whose component hazard ratios ran 0.24 to 0.54. For carcinoid-syndrome control the source is ENETS 2024, not these trials.",
        "Continue the somatostatin analogue for functional-syndrome control where it is needed, and after clinically significant progression in a nonfunctional tumour do not automatically continue it for antiproliferative benefit.",
        "C",
        "Functional disease, where the analogue is doing hormonal work that nothing else in the plan replaces.",
        "Carrying an analogue indefinitely in a nonfunctional tumour that has progressed on it, on the assumption that it is still holding the tumour back.",
        "Downgraded to C: this is a position taken in the absence of evidence rather than from it.         "Do not continue a somatostatin analogue for antiproliferative benefit in every nonfunctional NET after significant progression.",
        "Avoid",
        "B",
        "Continue it for hormonal control where the tumour is functional.",
        "PROMID and CLARINET tested delay of progression in stable, indolent disease — 96% of CLARINET patients had no progression in the 3 to 6 months before randomisation — and neither establishes an antiproliferative role after documented progression.",
        "Octreotide LAR or lanreotide",
        "PROMID: time to progression 14.3 versus 6 months with octreotide versus placebo in midgut NET. CLARINET established PFS benefit with lanreotide in nonfunctional enteropancreatic NET, Ki-67 <10%.",
        "CLARINET randomized double-blind trial, 204 nonfunctioning advanced enteropancreatic NET patients (101 lanreotide, 103 placebo).",
        "From randomization, median PFS not reached with lanreotide versus 18 months placebo; HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.30–0.73). Twenty-four-month PFS 65.1% versus 33.0%. No significant OS or QoL difference in the primary report. Diarrhea 26% versus 9%.",
        "Shows that stability and substantial survival without LT are plausible; does not estimate the added benefit of transplant or support treating all stable low-burden NET. G2 up to 20% and G3 are not represented by this <10% trial threshold."

{
 "slug": "crlm",
 "prefix": "CRLM",
 "questions": [
  {
   "id": "CRLM-D1",
   "n": 1,
   "question": "Name the accountable CRLM pathway owner and the neutral tumour-board chair.",
   "kind": "governance",
   "decisions": [],
   "positions": [],
   "divergence": "No source positions; programme decision.",
   "proposal": "The roadmap defines the roles but names no one: a neutral clinical chair synthesises one recommendation per case and names uncertainty instead of forcing consensus, programme leadership owns attendance, and this operating standard is shared with the HCC roadmap so one board runs one standard (grade D by construction).",
   "proposal_locator": "Operations · The board meeting ('Conference', 'Attendance' and closing note on shared HCC operating requirements)",
   "rationale": "The pathway produces one recommendation, one accountable owner, one due date and one reassessment plan; without a named owner and a neutral chair the synthesis step has nobody to perform it.",
   "audit": "Named individuals recorded in the programme charter, with the chair's name on every conference record."
  },
  {
   "id": "CRLM-D2",
   "n": 2,
   "question": "Approve the Epic submission form with an explicit phase field and a clearance-assessment field.",
   "kind": "operational",
   "decisions": [],
   "positions": [],
   "divergence": "No source positions; programme decision.",
   "proposal": "The Epic submission form should capture the clinical question, phase, disease extent, biology, prior treatment, transplant status, referring clinician and urgency; the clearance-discipline dashboard measure, the pathway's central claim, targets 95% or more of non-clearance decisions recording why each clearance route was unsuitable.",
   "proposal_locator": "Operations · The board meeting ('Submission'); The dashboard ('Clearance discipline')",
   "rationale": "Phase assignment and the explicit clearance question are the two things this pathway is built on, so they have to be captured at submission rather than reconstructed later.",
   "audit": "Completeness of the phase and clearance fields at triage; the clearance-discipline dashboard measure depends on them."
  },
  {
   "id": "CRLM-D3",
   "n": 3,
   "question": "Decide whether Memorial Hermann will run a hepatic arterial infusion programme, and if so the credentialing standard, case volume floor and toxicity review cadence.",
   "kind": "governance",
   "decisions": [
    "3",
    "5"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "NCCN Colon v2.2026",
     "ref": "nccn",
     "position": "Restricts HAI to patients with at least one prior systemic line and operative fitness, forbids concurrent bevacizumab or other VEGF inhibitors, and excludes prior liver radiation from HAI selection; early referral does not waive these eligibility rules.",
     "locator": "Gate 3 · Standard option 'Hepatic arterial infusion plus systemic therapy…' (pref, avoid); Gate 3 · Reasonable 'Selected Y90 radiation lobectomy…' (avoid)"
    },
    {
     "source": "Kemeny HAI conversion (phase I) and D’Angelica phase II",
     "ref": "19470932",
     "position": "Kemeny phase I: 49 patients, 47% conversion, 92% response; D'Angelica phase II (PMID 24646562): 49 patients, 47% conversion, 76% response. Roadmap critique: single-arm and centre-concentrated, neither a randomised conversion comparison; in the phase I series resectability was judged by the operating surgeons, response was WHO-type scored and median disease-free survival after R0 was only 7.6 months.",
     "locator": "What we are not sure about · 'Hepatic arterial infusion converts unresectable disease'; Gate 3 · HAI option (note)"
    },
    {
     "source": "Duke expanding-programme cohort",
     "ref": "39565488",
     "position": "In 102 mostly pretreated patients at a newer programme: 20% conversion, 23% HAI-specific complications and 6% biliary sclerosis; the roadmap says these selected-cohort results are not institutional performance targets.",
     "locator": "Gate 3 · HAI option (note); HAI evidence and pathway revision · 'Salvage evidence and external delivery'"
    },
    {
     "source": "Minimum requirements for new HAI programmes (international expert perspective)",
     "ref": "39962001",
     "position": "Credentialing must cover the whole service, not pump implantation alone: named surgeon and backup, oncologist, infusion nursing and pharmacy, perfusion assessment, IR rescue, refill coverage, toxicity escalation and an outcomes registry.",
     "locator": "HAI evidence and pathway revision · 'Programme readiness'"
    },
    {
     "source": "ESMO 2026",
     "ref": "41990853",
     "position": "Groups HAI with chemo- and radioembolisation as [III, C] intensification or salvage in liver-dominant disease; the roadmap criticises this for lumping HAI with modalities that failed in randomised trials and leaving no adjuvant route.",
     "locator": "Appendix: what is wrong with each paper · ESMO 2026"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "NCCN and the expert-programme paper treat HAI as a credentialed-centre therapy with defined eligibility while ESMO files it as low-grade salvage, and all conversion data are single-arm and centre-concentrated, so results at a new programme are uncertain.",
   "proposal": "The roadmap supports HAI plus systemic therapy (Standard, grade C, expertise-dependent) for selected unresectable liver-only CRLM at a credentialed pump centre, planned during first-line treatment rather than kept as terminal salvage, with the full service team, monitoring, toxicity escalation and an outcomes registry named before activation, and conversion recorded separately from pump response.",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 3 · Standard option 'Hepatic arterial infusion plus systemic therapy…'; HAI evidence and pathway revision · 'Earlier HAI review with a clearance endpoint', 'Programme readiness'",
   "rationale": "HAI conversion evidence is single-arm and concentrated in experienced centres, and biliary toxicity and pump complications are not occasional-case risks; the modality is only defensible with a credentialed programme behind it.",
   "audit": "Credentialing records, case volume against the floor, and the 6-month grade 3 or worse toxicity and biliary toxicity review."
  },
  {
   "id": "CRLM-D4",
   "n": 4,
   "question": "Ratify the written liver transplant protocol for CRLM: eligibility, review-board route, graft strategy including living donation, registry dataset and recurrence plan.",
   "kind": "governance",
   "decisions": [
    "4"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "OPTN transplant-oncology guidance (Dec 2025) and OPTN Policy 9",
     "ref": "optn-guidance",
     "position": "CRLM is not a standardised exception: listing needs nonstandard Adult Transplant Oncology Review Board review with the CRLM form and a narrative requesting MMaT-20, floored at 15 under Policy 9.4.E. The document is review-board guidance, not Policy.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Standard option 'Deceased-donor transplantation under the nonstandard review route' (when); Quick reference · transplant decision points"
    },
    {
     "source": "TransMet",
     "ref": "39306468",
     "position": "Intention-to-treat 5-year survival 56.6% versus 12.6% with chemotherapy. Roadmap critique: 19% never received a graft, 74% recurred, the gain rests on treating recurrence, and grafts came quickly only through negotiated national prioritisation.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Standard option 'Deceased-donor transplantation…' (when, note)"
    },
    {
     "source": "IHPBA 2021",
     "ref": "34506756",
     "position": "Permits extended-criteria grafts, machine perfusion and deceased- or living-donor RAPID; living donation only at centres meeting international benchmarks, preferably within a trial; no retransplantation for recurrent metastases.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Standard option 'Living-donor or RAPID graft strategy' (when)"
    },
    {
     "source": "North American LDLT series",
     "ref": "35353121",
     "position": "Ten of 91 evaluated patients transplanted at three centres, 1.5-year survival 100% and recurrence-free survival 62%. Roadmap critique: tiny, single-arm and short, non-transplanted patients unreported; the commentary calls it a technical demonstration.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · option 'Living-donor or RAPID graft strategy' (pref, note); What we are not sure about · 'Living-donor transplantation is an established route…'"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "The OPTN guidance supplies an allocation route but no graft or recurrence rules, IHPBA confines living donation to benchmark centres preferably in trials, and the living-donor evidence is short single-arm data, so the graft strategy rests on institutional judgement.",
   "proposal": "List first through the deceased-donor review-board route, where the randomised evidence and allocation pathway sit; treat living donation as a graft-supply answer at a benchmark programme with prospective entry, never a way around exception criteria; require a written protocol, transplant-oncology MDT, prospective registry and a recurrence plan agreed at selection; no ad hoc listing.",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 4 · Standard options (order) and 'Living-donor or RAPID graft strategy'; Gate 4 · Standard 'Keep the candidate inside protocol while waiting…'; Gate 4 · Avoid 'Ad hoc listing without auditable criteria…'",
   "rationale": "CRLM is not a standardised OPTN exception, so the institutional protocol is the operative constraint and the programme domain of the selection table requires it in writing.",
   "audit": "Protocol conformance and registry entry for every listed patient, reviewed quarterly."
  },
  {
   "id": "CRLM-D5",
   "n": 5,
   "question": "Set the institutional position on transplanting outside TransMet criteria — permitted under protocol with registry entry, or not at all.",
   "kind": "governance",
   "decisions": [
    "4"
   ],
   "positions": [
    {
     "source": "TransMet",
     "ref": "39306468",
     "position": "The only randomised evidence; it recruited 94 patients over 5.5 years at 20 centres after an independent panel rejected 40% of patients local boards had judged eligible, so nothing randomised exists outside that population.",
     "locator": "What we are not sure about · 'Transplantation should be offered beyond TransMet criteria'"
    },
    {
     "source": "Oslo cohort and SECA-II 10-year report",
     "ref": "37494056",
     "position": "Oslo score, CEA, largest lesion and metabolic tumour volume stratify survival strongly. Roadmap critique: one centre's thresholds, derived and tested in the same small cohorts, with no multivariable model; useful for counselling, not for relaxing eligibility.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Reasonable 'Use the Oslo score, the largest lesion diameter and PET metabolic tumour volume…' (pref, avoid, note)"
    },
    {
     "source": "ESMO 2026",
     "ref": "41990853",
     "position": "A looser filter: three or more months of stabilisation up to third line, with no MSI or PET-volume exclusion, so it would admit patients that IHPBA and the OPTN route bar.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Deceased-donor option (flagnote); What we are not sure about · 'There is one set of criteria…'"
    },
    {
     "source": "IHPBA 2021",
     "ref": "34506756",
     "position": "A stricter filter: adds metabolic-volume and lesion-glycolysis exclusions, bars MSI-high and dMMR patients, and requires six months of response; the roadmap notes none of these thresholds was validated in a large cohort.",
     "locator": "Gate 4 · Deceased-donor option (flagnote); What we are not sure about · 'There is one set of criteria…'"
    }
   ],
   "divergence": "No randomised evidence exists outside the TransMet population, ESMO's looser filter would admit patients IHPBA and the OPTN route exclude, and the prognostic scores that might justify extension are unvalidated single-centre work.",
   "proposal": "The roadmap leaves the either/or open but constrains it: a favourable prognostic score must not justify listing outside the protocol, any pathway beyond the guidance criteria needs its own approved protocol and may not be presented as exception-eligible, the stricter criteria govern, and a mandatory registry records whether criteria were met or exceeded.",
   "proposal_locator": "Gate 4 · Reasonable 'Use the Oslo score…' (avoid); Gate 4 · Avoid 'Ad hoc listing…'; Gate 4 · Deceased-donor option (flagnote); What we are not sure about · 'Transplantation should be offered beyond TransMet criteria'",
   "rationale": "There is no randomised evidence outside the TransMet population, and the roadmap lists this among the statements that are locally reasonable but not evidence based.",
   "audit": "Mandatory registry recording whether criteria were met or exceeded, recurrence site and post-recurrence survival."
  },
  {
   "id": "CRLM-D6",
   "n": 6,
   "question": "Define the pre-transplant checkpoint-inhibitor policy for MSI-high candidates, including washout and the approval route, before any such patient is listed.",
   "kind": "governance",

    "1",

   "positions": [

def item(text, *refs): return dict(text=text, refs=list(refs))
def nested(text, children, *refs): return dict(text=text, refs=list(refs), children=children)
def group(label, *items): return dict(label=label, items=list(items))
def branch(title, criteria, action, to=None, kind='advance', refs=()):
    return dict(title=title, criteria=criteria, action=action, to=to, kind=kind, refs=list(refs))
def step(id, title, question, owner, timing, orders, branches, stops=(), issues=()):
    return dict(id=id,title=title,question=question,owner=owner,timing=timing,orders=orders,branches=branches,stops=list(stops),issues=list(issues))
def comparison(ref, text, quote=False, locator=''):
    return dict(ref=ref,text=text,quote=quote,locator=locator)
def issue(id, question, comparisons, proposal, rationale, owners, record):
    return dict(id=id,question=question,comparisons=comparisons,proposal=proposal,rationale=rationale,owners=owners,record=record,status='Discussion required — not yet approved')
def pathway(slug,code,name,route,entry,roadmap,steps,issues):
    files=json.loads((ROOT.parent/'assets/documents.json').read_text())['tumors'][slug]['files']
    base=f'/mh-liver-pathways/documents/{slug}/'
    return dict(slug=slug,code=code,name=name,route=route,entry=entry,roadmap=roadmap,
                steps=steps,issues=issues,protocol=base+files['standard_info'],
                docs=[dict(label=label,url=base+files[slot]) for slot,label in [('decision','Decision discussion'),('standard_questions','Standard pathway questions')]])

"""Source-backed transplant decision pathways. Build with python3 src/build.py.

Clinical content is a review draft, not an automated eligibility determination.
References are attached to individual claims; local choices remain labelled draft.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import json

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
DIST = ROOT / 'dist'
POLICY = 'https://www.hrsa.gov/sites/default/files/hrsa/optn/optn_policies.pdf'
GUIDANCE = 'https://www.hrsa.gov/sites/default/files/hrsa/optn/adult-meld-exception-transplant-oncology-review-guidance.pdf'

def source(short, title, kind, locator, url, pattern=None, page=None, note=''):
    matches = sorted((DIST / 'evidence').rglob(pattern)) if pattern else []
    return dict(short=short, title=title, kind=kind, locator=locator, url=url,
                pdf=('/' + matches[0].relative_to(DIST).as_posix() + (f'#page={page}' if page else '')) if matches else url,

def item(text, *refs): return dict(text=text, refs=list(refs))
def nested(text, children, *refs): return dict(text=text, refs=list(refs), children=children)
def group(label, *items): return dict(label=label, items=list(items))
def branch(title, criteria, action, to=None, kind='advance', refs=()):
    return dict(title=title, criteria=criteria, action=action, to=to, kind=kind, refs=list(refs))
def step(id, title, question, owner, timing, orders, branches, stops=(), issues=()):
    return dict(id=id,title=title,question=question,owner=owner,timing=timing,orders=orders,branches=branches,stops=list(stops),issues=list(issues))
def comparison(ref, text, quote=False, locator=''):
    return dict(ref=ref,text=text,quote=quote,locator=locator)
def issue(id, question, comparisons, proposal, rationale, owners, record):
    return dict(id=id,question=question,comparisons=comparisons,proposal=proposal,rationale=rationale,owners=owners,record=record,status='Discussion required — not yet approved')
def pathway(slug,code,name,route,entry,roadmap,steps,issues):
    files=json.loads((ROOT.parent/'assets/documents.json').read_text())['tumors'][slug]['files']
    base=f'/mh-liver-pathways/documents/{slug}/'
    return dict(slug=slug,code=code,name=name,route=route,entry=entry,roadmap=roadmap,
                steps=steps,issues=issues,protocol=base+files['standard_info'],
                docs=[dict(label=label,url=base+files[slot]) for slot,label in [('decision','Decision discussion'),('standard_questions','Standard pathway questions')]])

def option(value, label, *details):
    return dict(value=value, label=label, details=list(details))

def question(id, label, options, refs, help='', criteria=()):
    return dict(id=id, label=label, options=options+[option('unknown','Uncertain / not yet assessed')],
                refs=list(refs), help=help, criteria=list(criteria))

def criterion(title, items, refs, show_for=()):
    return dict(title=title, items=items, refs=list(refs), show_for=list(show_for))

def rule(when, branch=None, kind=None, title=None, text=None, refs=()):
    return dict(when=when, branch=branch, kind=kind, title=title, text=text, refs=list(refs))

def pause(when, title, text, refs):
    return rule(when, kind='hold', title=title, text=text, refs=refs)

def stop(when, text, refs, title='Review the treatment and transplant plan'):
    return rule(when, kind='stop', title=title, text=text, refs=refs)

def yesno(id, label, refs, help='', yes='Yes', no='No'):
    return question(id,label,[option('yes',yes),option('no',no)],refs,help)

"""Essential, source-linked choices for the 46 existing transplant decisions.

These rules select a passage to review, not a transplant eligibility verdict.
Stop/clarification rules precede proceed rules. Every proceed rule specifies all
questions in that decision. No identifiers, raw clinical records or dates.
"""
VERSION = '2026-10-24.6'

def option(value, label, *details):
    return dict(value=value, label=label, details=list(details))

def question(id, label, options, refs, help='', criteria=()):
    return dict(id=id, label=label, options=options+[option('unknown','Uncertain / not yet assessed')],
                refs=list(refs), help=help, criteria=list(criteria))

def criterion(title, items, refs, show_for=()):
    return dict(title=title, items=items, refs=list(refs), show_for=list(show_for))

def rule(when, branch=None, kind=None, title=None, text=None, refs=()):
    return dict(when=when, branch=branch, kind=kind, title=title, text=text, refs=list(refs))

def pause(when, title, text, refs):
    return rule(when, kind='hold', title=title, text=text, refs=refs)

def stop(when, text, refs, title='Review the treatment and transplant plan'):
    return rule(when, kind='stop', title=title, text=text, refs=refs)

def yesno(id, label, refs, help='', yes='Yes', no='No'):
    return question(id,label,[option('yes',yes),option('no',no)],refs,help)
